A Clue to Solving the All-Solid-State Battery Lifespan Challenge [Reading Science] Hanyang University, Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute, and KIST Develop Bilayer Combining Silver-Carbon and Carbon Nanofiber Layers Capacity Retained at 92% After 250 Charge-Discharge Cycles...11.2 Percentage Points Higher Than Existing Structure Expansion during charging and contraction during discharging are among the main causes of shortened service life in all-solid-state batteries, a next-generation battery technology. Korean researchers have developed a bilayer structure that evenly distributes lithium inside the battery and absorbs volume changes, helping to mitigate the problem of capacity degradation. The National Research Foundation of Korea announced on November 17 that a joint research team led by Professor Lee Jongwon of Hanyang University, Principal Researcher Choi Jeonghee of the Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute, and Principal Researcher Jung Hoonki of the Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST) had developed a new bilayer structure that mitigates volume changes during the charging and discharging of anode-free all-solid-state batteries. Fabrication process of a double-layer all-solid-state battery and its lithium storage mechanism. (a) Fabrication of the double-layer structure combining a silver-carbon layer and a carbon nanofiber layer. (b) Lithium stored inside the carbon nanofiber layer and between the two layers after charging. (c) Reduction in internal pressure fluctuations achieved by applying the double-layer structure. (d) How sequential lithium storage mitigates volume expansion and mechanical stress. Provided by the research team led by Professor Lee Jongwon of Hanyang University. View original image All-solid-state batteries are a next-generation battery technology that can reduce fire risks by replacing the liquid electrolyte in conventional lithium-ion batteries with a solid electrolyte. Anode-free all-solid-state batteries, in particular, can reduce weight and volume and increase energy density because they do not use a separate anode active material, such as graphite, during manufacturing. The technology has attracted attention for its potential to extend the driving range of electric vehicles, but volume changes during charging and discharging have been considered a barrier to commercialization. During charging, lithium ions that have moved from the cathode gain electrons and accumulate as metallic lithium, increasing the battery's internal volume. During discharging, the accumulated lithium turns back into ions and moves, reducing the volume. Repetition of this process can destabilize contact between the electrode and solid electrolyte and cause mechanical damage inside the battery, potentially shortening its service life. To address this issue, the team designed a bilayer structure combining a thin silver-carbon layer with a carbon nanofiber layer containing abundant internal voids. The silver-carbon layer guides lithium to accumulate evenly rather than concentrating in specific areas during the initial stage of charging. As more lithium flows in, the carbon nanofiber layer stores it in its internal voids, mitigating volume expansion. By tracking lithium migration and accumulation through structural analysis and computer simulations, the team found that lithium first accumulates in the silver-carbon layer during the initial stage of charging, then fills the voids in the carbon nanofiber layer, and subsequently accumulates between the two layers. Capacity Maintained at 92% After 250 Charge-Discharge Cycles When the bilayer structure was applied to an actual pouch cell, the cell retained 92.0% of its initial capacity after 250 charge-discharge cycles, even at the relatively low pressure of 2 megapascals (MPa). This was 11.2 percentage points higher than the capacity retention rate of a cell using only the existing silver-carbon layer (80.8%). The results demonstrated the potential to improve battery service life by mitigating mechanical damage caused by charging and discharging. The joint research team that developed a bilayer structure for all-solid-state batteries. From left: Professor Lee Jongwon of Hanyang University; Principal Researcher Choi Jeonghee of the Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute; Principal Researcher Jung Hoonki of the Korea Institute of Science and Technology; and co-first authors Kang Junhee and Lee Taeyoung. Photo courtesy of the National Research Foundation of Korea. View original image However, these results were verified under experimental conditions. Before the technology can be applied to actual electric vehicle batteries, stable performance must be achieved in large-area, stacked cells, and long-term charge-discharge durability must be further validated. “This study is significant because it presents a new approach that goes beyond existing technologies for promoting uniform lithium deposition and can also mitigate mechanical damage during charging and discharging,” Professor Lee said. “We plan to develop the technology to deliver stable performance in large-area, stacked all-solid-state batteries and enable long-term operation at room temperature and under low-pressure conditions.” Hot Picks Today "Two Spend 500,000 Won in a Flash, Yet Wait Two Hours?" ... artigo.texto: Charge Power has been appointed to manage two Texas battery energy storage projects totalling 290MW/580MWh through commissioning and into commercial operation in 2027. The two projects comprise a 150MW/300MWh BESS and a 140MW/280MWh system, both connecting to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) grid. Charge Power will act as an owner’s-side project partner rather than as battery supplier or EPC contractor. Its role will be to coordinate the engineering, procurement and construction contractors, project engineers, equipment suppliers, documentation and grid-connection requirements needed to take both projects from late-stage construction through commissioning to commercial operation date, or COD. COD is the point at which a project has completed the required testing and contractual milestones and can begin normal commercial operation and earn revenue. For projects in ERCOT, the process also involves completing the grid operator’s interconnection and commissioning requirements before the asset can participate fully in the Texas electricity market. Both projects will also use the WARAM platform for project governance, due diligence and compliance. Charge Power said the software is intended to link physical asset requirements with the documentation and evidence needed to demonstrate that those requirements have been met throughout ownership, certification and eventual asset transfer. Founder and president Ravi Pinnelli said: “Texas is one of the most demanding storage markets in the country, and the stretch between construction and commercial operation is where a project either protects its returns or loses them. “We approach every project with an owner-operator mindset, so on these projects our decisions prioritize schedule, revenue, and long-term performance the way the owner would. “Through shifting markets and an evolving energy landscape, our goal is to deliver execution certainty from day one to COD and beyond.” Charge Power said it has commissioned 3GW/7GWh of energy storage since the company was founded in 2022. The company works across US electricity markets including ERCOT, CAISO, MISO and PJM, as well as projects in Canada, India, Japan and the UK. Battery storage deployment has grown rapidly in Texas as developers seek to capture low-cost electricity during periods of abundant generation and discharge it during higher-priced periods of demand. Charge Power cited Modo Energy figures showing ERCOT battery capacity reached 16.5GW/28.8GWh by the end of June 2026, following rapid annual growth since 2020. BESTmag has previously reported on a number of large Texas projects, including Eolian’s 400MW/1.8GWh Padua BESS complex and Energy Vault’s 57MW/114MWh Cross Trails system. The chemistry and equipment suppliers for Charge Power’s two newly awarded projects were not disclosed. Photo: Charge Power’s 240MW/480MWh Anole BESS in Texas. artigo.texto: EcoPro is stepping up efforts to strengthen its global competitiveness by showcasing its secondary battery materials ecosystem in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province, and its next-generation battery materials technologies. EcoPro said Sunday that it participated in the International Battery Expo 2026 Pohang, held for three days from Nov. 13 at Manindang Gymnasium in Pohang. Now in its second year, the expo is a specialized exhibition showcasing technologies and future visions across the entire battery industry, from materials and components to recycling used batteries. EcoPro organized its exhibition booth around seven themes, including cooperation with the Pohang community, global supply chains, high-nickel cathode materials and next-generation battery materials. Since 2017, EcoPro has invested approximately 3.3 trillion won in Pohang to build a secondary battery materials ecosystem linking precursor and cathode material production with used battery recycling. The company is strengthening its supply chain competitiveness through a closed-loop system that connects raw material procurement, production and recycling. The company also introduced its global production network. It is building an integrated supply chain linking its BNSI nickel smelter in Indonesia, its cathode materials plant in Debrecen, Hungary, and its domestic production facilities, connecting raw material sourcing with finished product manufacturing. EcoPro also showcased its next-generation battery materials technologies. Its lineup included high-nickel ternary cathode materials, known for their high energy density, as well as mid-nickel cathode materials, materials for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials. The company also presented its solid electrolyte technology, a key material for all-solid-state batteries, outlining its strategy to expand its product portfolio. High-nickel cathode materials, in particular, are expected to find wider applications beyond electric vehicles in emerging industries requiring high energy density, including humanoid robots, urban air mobility (UAM) and aerospace. EcoPro also highlighted its contributions to the local community. Through social initiatives such as supporting childbirth in vulnerable households, providing safety umbrellas for children and developing community welfare villages, the company has been recognized as a community-contributing company for seven consecutive years. "Having grown in Pohang, EcoPro feels a strong responsibility to contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of Korea's battery industry alongside the local community," EcoPro CEO Choi Sang-woon said. "We will do our utmost to boost our global competitiveness through continued investment and technological innovation while helping revitalize the local economy and create quality jobs."

artigo.texto: SamsungSDI has secured an additional supply volume of LFP (lithium iron phosphate) batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) worth 3 to 4 trillion won from U.S.-based Jupiter Power, signaling a major step in expanding its medium- and long-term order book. After already securing production volumes through 2028, the company has also landed large-scale, long-term contracts starting in 2029, broadening its growth foundation in the U.S. ESS market. As of the 16th, SamsungSDI's cumulative U.S. power ESS order book has grown to over 76 GWh (gigawatt-hours), including an additional 16 GWh contract with Jupiter Power. The existing order volume of more than 60 GWh secured by the end of October this year alone is sufficient to keep the U.S. SPE (Star Plus Energy) and Ulsan production lines running at full capacity through 2028. This new contract covers supply over three years starting in 2029, marking another achievement for SamsungSDI in securing long-term supply volumes. To meet growing ESS demand, SamsungSDI is accelerating the expansion of its local production capacity in the United States. In early October, the company began mass production of prismatic LFP batteries for ESS at its SPE plant in Indiana, and started shipping battery cells from mid-October. The produced cells will undergo module and battery box processes before being delivered to customers as finished SBB (Samsung Battery Box) products starting in December. SamsungSDI is working to expand supply capacity by converting existing electric vehicle (EV) battery production lines into ESS LFP battery facilities. It is additionally converting two of the four production lines at its U.S. SPE Plant 1. The company also plans to utilize the U.S. Synergy Cells plant, acquired through the full buyout of its joint venture stake with GM (General Motors) in August, as an ESS production hub. Synergy Cells is currently optimizing designs to convert existing EV facilities into high-capacity LFP battery production lines for ESS. Mass production is scheduled to begin from late 2028 to early 2029, followed by phased expansion of production lines. This expansion of the ESS business is also closely tied to efforts to capture the battery market for AI (artificial intelligence) data centers. SamsungSDI is accelerating its market push by leveraging its status as the world's only company capable of supplying all three essential battery solutions for data centers: BESS (battery energy storage systems), UPS (uninterruptible power supplies), and BBU (battery backup units). As a result, performance has shown signs of recovery. SamsungSDI's cumulative operating profit for the first three quarters of this year reached 456 billion won, turning profitable compared to an operating loss of 1.4232 trillion won in the same period last year. Building on its improved performance, SamsungSDI is strategizing to accelerate its next-generation all-solid-state battery business. All-solid-state batteries use solid electrolytes instead of liquid ones, offering enhanced safety. The company is developing the technology with a target of commercialization in the second half of next year. Since September, it has been supplying all-solid-state battery cell and pack samples for humanoid robots to multiple customers for performance evaluation. It is currently at the stage of refining product specifications for next year's mass production through iterative performance improvements and verification based on customer requirements. The company is also working in parallel to establish a stable supply chain for key materials such as cathode materials and solid electrolytes. A SamsungSDI official stated, "This order reflects recognition of our global technological competitiveness by securing large volumes early on," adding, "We will continue to lead the market with products that combine the performance and safety required by customers."

artigo.texto: As far as we know, San Francisco has three data centers. Two are in Bayview, and one is in Soma. They’re relatively small in terms of energy and water use. The two associated places on Paul Avenue have been around for decades, since the days when we called them “server farms.” The City Planning Department admits other centers may exist, on a smaller scale, since the department has no formal inventory of this type of land use. The Board of Supes recently approved a 45-day moratorium on new centers, and the Land Use and Transportation Committee will consider Monday/16 a year-long extension. The Planning Department has done a study on the issue, and its findings suggests that the city needs at least a moratorium, if not an outright ban. From an environmental justice perspective, data centers are a public nuisance—and to no surprise, all are in low-income neighborhoods with high concentrations of people of color. I don’t think we’re going to see a data center in Pacific Heights. The city also has a major capacity problem. According to the report, big data centers use as much as 50 megawatts of power, which is enough for 25,000 homes. The city’s under immense pressure to approve more housing—and the grid doesn’t have much space available. The current capacity of the power lines coming into San Francisco is 1 gigawatt. Peak usage is about 900 megawatts, and that’s rising, as more residents, businesses, and vehicles are shifting to electric power. A 50 MW data center would overwhelm the grid. PG&E can’t handle this load. Expanding the power lines coming into San Francisco could take at least eight years, and would cost hundreds of millions of dollars. If the city had a municipal utility, it could control new data centers: The City of Santa Clara, which already has 55 existing data centers, has its own municipal utility (Silicon Valley Power, SVP) that stopped taking new applications for service from data centers (but not other development) in 2023 while it assessed the ability to provide power for these uses and while they await the completion of a major transmission expansion project expected to be completed in the next couple years. Then there’s water. From the report: SFPUC has concerns for existing and potential future data centers about the types of chemicals (and their concentrations and amounts) that are being used for cooling systems; whether wastewater discharges from data centers are within the local temperature limit of 125 °F; and whether the combined sewer system has the capacity to handle the data center’s wastewater flow, especially during wet weather. Depending on the water quality, there’s a risk of causing additional corrosion to sewers. SFPUC uses site-specific wastewater discharge permits to regulate non-domestic and temporary discharges into the City’s combined sewer system. Mayor Daniel Lurie loves AI, and if the companies he sees as the city’s economic future want local data centers, I suspect he will by sympathetic. Of course, it we don’t build them here, we’re just outsourcing the problem to other communities. The committee will consider the planning report Monday/16, and the full board will discuss a year-long moratorium Tuesday/17. I don’t use self-checkout. I hate having to take pictures of checks on my phone and sending them to the bank. People used to get paid to do that work; now they’ve lost their jobs, and I’m supposed to do it, for no pay. It’s hard to find an open bank branch with real tellers these days, and sometimes it costs money to get a human on the phone for customer service. When I have an internet outage, my provider’s phone system tells me to seek help on the web; dude, I can’t get to the web. That’s the problem. Not everyone is young and tech-savvy. Some people need people, real people, to help them with their groceries or prescriptions or banking. And the more technology replaces people, the more we are going to have to deal with massive unemployment. The Government Audit and Oversight Committee will consider Thursday/19 a measure that would place limits on self-checkout facilities at grocery stores and pharmacies. The measure would require one employee-staffed checkout center for every three self-check centers, would limit self-check to 15 items, and would mandate one employee to supervise every self-check operations center. The measure has six co-sponsors, enough to ensure it will pass, but not enough to override a mayoral veto. That hearing starts at 10am. Thanks to the AI boom and radical economic inequality, evictions are soaring in San Francisco; landlords are looking for any possible loophole to get rid of rent-controlled tenants who are paying below market rate. One tactic: Cite a “nuisance.” Some landlords in Chinatown tried to use that tool to evict renters who hung their laundry out to dry on a clothesline. It’s been used to evict tenants who have bicycles in public spaces. The Land Use and Transportation Committee will consider Monday/16 an ordinance that would restrict “nuisance” evictions. Among other things, it would ban evictions for damage to the property if the tenants paid to have the place repaired. That hearing starts at 10 am. A final note: I’m not surprised that the Chron would allow the head of a hotel lobbying group to write an oped promoting the economic interests of the giants of the hospitality industry. I’m not even surprised by the doom-and-gloom rhetoric: If this amendment were to pass, unions would be able to hold hotels and the city hostage, and San Francisco’s hospitality and reputational recovery would come to a screeching halt. The union and its representatives would be able to use the threat of a legal filing to gain leverage with hotels during contract negotiations. As a result, investments in new hotels and investments in renovations will dry up, and San Francisco will become a no-invest zone once again. But this is still a union town, and language like this is a bit shocking: Yet the full Board of Supervisors

artigo.texto: In the electric vehicle (EV) battery market, where Korean batteries are under pressure, they have yet to find a breakthrough for a turnaround. As the rise of "Made in China" batteries continues, voices are growing that a counteroffensive must be launched centered on new product lineups such as mid-nickel, lithium manganese-rich (LMR), and all-solid-state batteries. According to battery industry sources and Samsung Securities on Tuesday, CATL's share of Hyundai Motor Group's EV sales was 29% as of September last year. This figure represents a 16 percentage point (p) increase compared to the same period last year. In contrast, during the same period, SK On's share decreased from 52% to 38%, and LG Energy Solution's share fell from 32% to 30%. A similar trend is observed among other automakers. Currently, within the Volkswagen Group, Korean battery makers hold a 53% market share, while Chinese firms account for approximately 45%, according to analysis. The Volkswagen Group, which had used almost 100% Korean batteries, newly adopted CATL batteries in the first half of 2024. In less than three years since then, the market share of Chinese batteries has closed in on that of K-batteries. Jo Hyeon-ryeol, a researcher at Samsung Securities, explained, "With China's Gotion also entering the Volkswagen Group's supply chain this year, it is expected that K-batteries will cede the lead to Chinese firms by 2027." He added, "Similarly, as Hyundai Motor Group has fully launched new vehicles equipped with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries—an area where China holds an advantage—the market share of Chinese companies is likely to expand further." K-batteries are aiming to increase sales of EV batteries in the United States, where a "No China Zone" has been established, but this too is proving difficult. This is due to the shrinking front-end market resulting from the second Trump administration's abolition of EV purchase subsidies. Through the third quarter last year, GM's EV sales were approximately 214,000 units, and Ford's were about 221,000 units, representing year-on-year declines of 15.6% and 4.4%, respectively. Both companies are experiencing their first negative growth trend since 2020. Domestic battery majors such as LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On have adopted a strategy of weathering the EV market downturn by expanding sales of batteries for energy storage systems (ESS). However, as the strength of Chinese firms led by LFP becomes more pronounced year by year, there are concerns that K-batteries may lose their lead in the EV battery market, which is considered the industry's "main battlefield." CATL and others are leveraging cost competitiveness to target not only the LFP segment, where they have shown superiority, but also the ternary cathode market, which has been a stronghold for K-batteries. For K-batteries, it is urgent to regroup and secure market share in the EV battery sector. LG Energy Solution is increasing sales of high-voltage mid-nickel batteries, a mid-to-low-priced product that can serve as a check against Chinese-made LFP, centered on its Poland plant. LMR, which offers higher energy density at a price similar to LFP, is also considered a promising candidate. LG Energy Solution is pushing for the production of next-generation LMR prismatic batteries through Ultium Cells, its joint venture with GM. Whether all-solid-state batteries can emerge as a "game changer" is also a key issue. In the development of all-solid-state batteries, known as the "dream battery" for maximizing performance and safety through solid electrolytes, Samsung SDI is assessed to be in the lead. The company's goal is to mass-produce all-solid-state batteries within next year and apply them to EVs following their use in humanoid robots. A battery industry official said, "Even if we perform well in the ESS market, ceding the EV market to China would inevitably result in a significant blow." He added, "We must be able to create a turning point in the EV battery market next year."

artigo.texto: Essa informação foi compartilhada pelo Sr. Bui Duc Hieu, Diretor Adjunto do Departamento de Mudanças Climáticas, com a imprensa em um evento de lançamento online realizado à margem da 31ª Conferência das Partes da Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (COP31), em Antalya, Turquia, no dia 13 de novembro. Segundo ele, o desenvolvimento de um mercado de carbono é uma das soluções para apoiar a implementação dos compromissos nacionais de resposta às mudanças climáticas, especialmente a meta de alcançar emissões líquidas zero até 2050. “Constatamos que um mercado de carbono não é apenas uma ferramenta para gerenciar emissões, mas também precisa criar incentivos para que as empresas inovem em tecnologia, melhorem a eficiência energética e invistam em soluções de redução de emissões”, afirmou o Sr. Hieu. No contexto da implementação acelerada do Acordo de Paris sobre mudanças climáticas em todo o mundo , os mercados de carbono estão se tornando uma ferramenta política crucial para promover a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa, mobilizar recursos para transições verdes e apoiar o cumprimento dos compromissos internacionais. De acordo com representantes do Departamento de Mudanças Climáticas, o Vietnã encontra-se atualmente nos estágios iniciais de implementação de um sistema de comércio de emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Portanto, é necessário buscar recomendações e experiências de outros países e parceiros internacionais em relação à gestão, monitoramento e operação dos mercados de carbono para atingir a meta de operação oficial do mercado até 2029. O Vietnã fez progressos significativos no aperfeiçoamento de sua estrutura institucional e na construção da infraestrutura para seu mercado de carbono. 2026 também marca uma transição crucial do desenvolvimento de políticas para a implementação prática. Até o momento, o Vietnã alocou cotas de emissão de gases de efeito estufa para 110 instalações nos setores de energia térmica, siderurgia e cimento para o período de 2025-2026 e colocou em operação o Sistema Nacional de Registro de Cotas de Emissão de Gases de Efeito Estufa e Créditos de Carbono. Notavelmente, a bolsa de carbono doméstica foi oficialmente lançada em 29 de junho na Bolsa de Valores de Hanói . No entanto, estabelecer um novo quadro legal e infraestrutura técnica é apenas o começo. De acordo com o vice-diretor Bui Duc Hieu, durante a fase piloto, o Vietnã precisa continuar aprimorando o sistema de medição, reporte e avaliação das emissões de gases de efeito estufa, além de garantir a coordenação sincronizada entre os órgãos de gestão e os operadores de mercado, e fortalecer a capacidade e a prontidão das empresas para participar. Esses são os requisitos que precisam ser atendidos para que o mercado de carbono se torne, de fato, uma ferramenta eficaz para promover a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Ao elogiar o progresso do Vietnã na tradução do compromisso em ação, John Robert Cotton, Diretor da Parceria para a Transição Energética do Sudeste Asiático (ETP), afirmou que poucos países conseguem fazer a transição de um arcabouço legal para a operação de um mercado de carbono obrigatório em tão pouco tempo quanto o Vietnã. Enfatizando a importância da precificação do carbono para incorporar os custos de emissão aos balanços patrimoniais das empresas, Cotton disse que, a partir de 2029, quando o mecanismo de leilão de cotas começar a ser implementado, o mercado gerará receita para o orçamento do Estado, que poderá então ser reinvestida em atividades de redução de emissões na indústria. Segundo ele, "gargalos" semelhantes que dificultam o funcionamento do mercado também estão sendo encontrados em muitos outros países da região. "Nas Filipinas , a ETP está auxiliando o Ministério das Finanças na realização de uma revisão jurídica dos instrumentos de precificação de carbono. Na Indonésia, estamos trabalhando com o Ministério do Comércio e o Ministério da Indústria para avaliar o impacto das exportações de ferro e aço, cimento, alumínio e fertilizantes nos mecanismos tributários internacionais", afirmou. Reconhecendo o progresso significativo do Vietnã no desenvolvimento de seu mercado de carbono, a Sra. Leticia Guimarães, Chefe da Unidade de Mercado Global de Carbono do PNUD Vietnã, enfatizou: “O Vietnã estabeleceu uma estrutura legal clara e robusta para seu mercado de carbono. O lançamento da Bolsa em junho reafirmou sua posição como um dos países pioneiros na região da ASEAN. Também estamos muito satisfeitos com o lançamento do Portal de Informações de Mercado, que ajuda a divulgar informações importantes, lançando as bases para que as partes interessadas e os investidores tenham confiança nas próximas etapas.”

artigo.texto: HD Hyundai Energy Solution and HD Hyundai Electric said Monday that they will jointly participate in 'RE+ 26,' North America's largest clean energy exhibition, held at the Las Vegas Convention Center in the United States, showcasing their integrated energy business capabilities spanning from solar power generation to energy storage, conversion, and transmission and distribution. HD Hyundai Energy Solution will unveil its 'TOPCon Multi-Cut (G12R TOPCon Multi-Cut)' module for the North American market for the first time. Multi-cut is a technology that divides large-area solar cells into multiple pieces to reduce power loss generated during current flow. Through this, the company achieved a module efficiency of 24.4% by increasing power density. It plans to gradually apply ultra-precision multi-cut technology to its production lines to strengthen the competitiveness of its high-efficiency products. HD Hyundai Electric will introduce battery energy storage systems (BESS) and power grid stabilization technologies. The company will showcase major domestic and international project cases, including the 96th-megawatt-class Anmyeondo BESS project in Sinan, South Korea, and the 100th-megawatt-class Rutile BESS project in Texas, United States. It will also present Grid-Forming technology, which actively controls voltage and frequency to enhance power supply stability, as well as a product lineup of power equipment targeting the North American power grid and data center markets. In the United States, the utilization of energy storage systems is rapidly increasing alongside the expansion of solar power generation. According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), U.S. solar power generation increased by 18.3% year-on-year from January to August this year. More than 16% of new large-scale solar facilities built through September this year were installed together with battery storage systems. The importance of grid stabilization technology and the expansion of transmission and distribution infrastructure is also growing due to increasing power demand and the expanded integration of renewable energy into the power grid. The two companies are strengthening their business foundations for targeting the North American market. HD Hyundai Electric is expanding its local business base through the expansion of its North American production subsidiary and the expansion of its BESS business via its Texas subsidiary. HD Hyundai Energy Solution is responding to changes in U.S. supply chain regulations, including requirements related to Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC), based on its domestic integrated cell and module production system. An official from HD Hyundai said, "In the North American market, not only product technological capability but also stable supply capacity and project execution capabilities have emerged as key competitive factors." He added, "Taking this exhibition as an opportunity, we will expand cooperation with local customers and partners and discover practical business opportunities."

artigo.texto: The Greek energy group targets 1 GW of renewable generation and 500 MW of battery storage by 2030, highlighting the growing importance of grid flexibility and energy storage in renewable infrastructure development. HELLENiQ ENERGY plans to invest more than €1 billion in Romania by 2030, expanding its solar, wind and battery energy storage operations as part of its regional growth strategy. The company aims to reach 1 GW of installed renewable generation capacity and 500 MW of battery energy storage system (BESS) power capacity, positioning Romania as its second-largest renewable energy growth market after Greece. The investment program forms part of the group’s Vision 2035+ strategy and reflects a broader transformation of its energy portfolio, in which renewable generation is increasingly linked to storage infrastructure and electricity grid integration. A renewable portfolio combining solar and wind assets HELLENiQ ENERGY currently operates four photovoltaic parks in the Romanian counties of Teleorman, Giurgiu, Olt and Dolj, with a combined installed capacity of 211 MW. These facilities generate electricity equivalent to the annual consumption of more than 155,000 households. The portfolio will be expanded with a 96 MW wind farm in Galați County, scheduled for completion in the second quarter of 2027. Additional wind and solar projects at advanced development stages exceed 500 MW of renewable generation capacity, alongside another 500 MW of planned battery storage power capacity. This combination of technologies is intended to diversify generation profiles and reduce dependence on a single renewable energy source. Battery storage becomes central to the generation strategy The planned 500 MW of BESS capacity represents one of the main components of the company’s Romanian expansion. Battery systems can absorb electricity during periods of high renewable generation and discharge it when demand increases or market conditions become more favorable. However, storage power capacity alone does not determine how much energy a battery installation can deliver. Its actual storage capability depends on the installed energy capacity, measured in megawatt-hours (MWh), and its discharge duration. HELLENiQ previously identified a potential Romanian storage configuration of 500 MW and 1,500 MWh. The company has also been assessing battery integration into existing photovoltaic assets through a potential 170 MW / 680 MWh installation. These developments illustrate how battery storage can be incorporated into both new hybrid renewable projects and operating solar facilities. Grid connection constraints influence project economics One of the most important aspects of the expansion concerns electricity infrastructure. According to reporting by Romanian energy publication Energynomics, based on statements from company executives, two recently completed photovoltaic parks initially operated with restrictions on electricity injection while additional grid reinforcement works were being carried out. This highlights an important distinction in renewable project development: completing a generating facility does not necessarily guarantee immediate access to the full available grid connection capacity. Battery storage can help manage excess generation and shift electricity delivery toward periods of higher commercial value. However, it cannot replace the transmission infrastructure upgrades required to accommodate additional renewable capacity. For HELLENiQ ENERGY, reaching its 2030 targets in Romania will therefore depend not only on project construction, but also on grid access, operational availability and the ability to commercialize the electricity generated. artigo.texto: Two days of training end with a diploma reception. Companies eager to hire the new graduates have come ready to hand out jobs that can pay more than $100,000 a year. Welcome to the data center economy. In the race to build out America’s AI infrastructure, tech companies are struggling to find technicians with sufficient skills to install the cooling, server racks, electrical equipment and fiberoptic cables necessary to meet the off-the-charts demand for the revolutionary technology. Even as AI politics have shifted – particularly after recent midterm election – the lack of available labor to build continuing data center projects would almost certainly trump any potential construction slowdown. So the industry is going to extraordinary lengths to teach and hire people to fill those crucial jobs. Several nonprofits, online learning companies and all four of the big AI hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft — offer various forms of free, accelerated training courses for the technical skills needed to build out data centers. Some of those positions can pay six-figure salaries. And many Americans don’t even know these jobs exist. Graduation on Friday. Orientation on Monday Javonntae Hill studied video game design. He’s in his early 30s and he was looking for a career — but didn’t quite know where to start. His girlfriend saw an advertisement for America’s Workforce Academy, a new training program Meta kicked off in August to help fill the labor skills gap. The company was willing to pay him during his four-week training and guaranteed him placement in a data center job after he received his diploma. Hill figured he’d give it a shot. Over the course of a month, in a classroom of 30 people, he got thrown into a mix of lectures and hands-on training, learning about how to place and run fiberoptic and copper cables and what each cable insulator color specifies. He was nervous: He hoped he could retain all that information for his new job. “Graduation was on Friday,” Hill said. “I started orientation on Monday.” Meta partnered with Associated Builders and Contractors, a construction industry trade group that has been training workers for decades. Unlike traditional training methods, including trade school or an apprenticeship, ABC’s accelerated courses aren’t designed to be comprehensive; they’re designed to get as many people working in data centers as possible. “It’s like the military,” said Joel Thames, head of ABC’s safety and workforce group. “Does boot camp get them trained for any scenario? No. But it gives them a foundational education before they spend time on the job site.” Hill said his nerves were unfounded: He showed up to the Ohio job site overprepared. And grateful. “I could do this for the rest of my life,” Hill said. “I’ve seen postings of jobs available, but I have a lot of loyalty toward Meta.” The problem Despite growing public opposition and a wave of new lawmakers pledging to regulate their expansion, data center construction is virtually unstoppable. AI infrastructure spending is expected to approach $1 trillion a year, annually for the foreseeable future, according to Columbia Business School economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. But construction faces many logistical hurdles, including building permits, power guarantees, materials and financing. Even the deepest-pocketed AI companies that can overcome those obstacles are encountering a consistent roadblock: America has far too few qualified people to build data centers — particularly in some of the remote or rural locations where they’re being built. The United States has a shortage of 1 million engineers needed to meet data center construction estimates, PwC estimates. Many otherwise ready-to-go sites have been delayed for months while they assemble a qualified crew to build them. Only about half of the AI computing capacity scheduled to come online between now and 2028 is actually expected to meet its target date, according to Goldman Sachs. That’s a costly wait: For large AI data centers, a month of delay can cost anywhere from the low tens of millions to well over $100 million, depending on location, scale and contract terms, said Mona Dajani, co-chair of Cooley’s infrastructure, energy and real estate practice. So AI companies are addressing the challenge by ditching requirements for multi-year trade school courses or apprenticeships in favor of accelerated, high-intensity courses designed specifically for data center construction jobs. Many are offering the courses for free. A growing number will even pay learners to take the courses. Classes can run from 15 weeks to just two days, depending on the job. Desperation for labor is so high that AI companies are placing some top graduates on the job the day after they gain their certifications. ‘I had nothing to lose’ Robert Burgess had been bouncing around construction jobs in and around Canton, Mississippi. He knew how to do some low-voltage electrical work and had heard that he could make a lot more money cutting fiber for a telecom or a data center site. Burgess Googled “internet fiber training Mississippi” and a four-week Amazon training program called I2PA (Information Infrastructure Pre-Apprenticeship) surfaced at a local community college. “I had nothing to lose,” Burgess said. “I put in my email, and I got accepted.” Over the course of the training, Burgess learned how electricity is generated and delivered, how servers are installed and how they fit into a data center. Amazon trainers set up a mock data center so that Burgess and his classmates could get hands-on training. At the end: a job fair. Burgess got a job from Yates Construction and Turner Construction, which were partnering on the tail end of a data center construction site in the area. That was in 2024. artigo.texto: O governo dos Estados Unidos emitiu uma norma nesta segunda-feira, 16, que deve dificultar a aquisição de chips de Inteligência Artificial (IA) por empresas de data centers sediadas em cinco países, entre eles o Brasil. A norma publicada pelo Departamento de Comércio não proíbe a compra de chips. Contudo, estabelece que Brasil, Indonésia, Malásia, Singapura e Tailândia deverão obter, além das exigências de licenciamento atualmente em vigor para semicondutores avançados, uma licença adicional para exportação, reexportação ou transferência de chips de alta capacidade. Embora tenha listado cinco países, o governo de Donald Trump busca, na prática, atingir a China com a medida. A ideia é dificultar que empresas chinesas utilizem data centers em outros países para processar demandas de alta capacidade computacional usando tecnologia norte-americana. Conforme a norma, o Brasil e as demais nações são classificados pelo governo dos Estados Unidos como "países que apresentam um risco de desvio superior ao normal". Nesse sentido, a medida afirma que data centers que forneçam um volume significativo de poder computacional a empresas sediadas na China ou em países do chamado grupo D:5 (mercados sujeitos a embargos de armas dos Estados Unidos) deverão obter uma licença no prazo de 90 dias, sob pena de enfrentar futuras restrições à exportação. De acordo com a medida, a exigência de licença não alcança semicondutores destinados a empresas sediadas nos Estados Unidos ou cuja controladora final esteja sediada no território norte-americano. "A norma visa a garantir que as restrições já existentes ao acesso a tecnologias norte-americanas sensíveis não possam ser contornadas por meio de arranjos de computação remota que envolvam data centers em países terceiros", afirma o Departamento de Comércio, em comunicado. A nota oficial ainda afirma que os Estados Unidos "estão empenhados em promover a adoção global de tecnologia norte-americana para fins comerciais legítimos". Sendo assim, o governo busca atuar para que "tecnologias sensíveis não sejam exploradas por meios que ameacem a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos". Pontos de atenção Em comunicado, a Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Software (Abes) afirma que "acompanha com atenção" a medida anunciada pelo governo norte-americano. A entidade destacou que a norma, enquanto representa uma nova camada de compliance para subsidiárias de empresas sediadas nos Estados Unidos, gera uma "assimetria competitiva" para provedores de nuvem e data centers de capital nacional, por exigir autorizações analisadas caso a caso. Além disso, para a Abes, a inclusão do Brasil em uma lista restritiva pode dificultar a atração de novos investimentos internacionais ao setor de infraestrutura digital brasileiro. Desse modo, a associação defende uma atuação coordenada entre o governo brasileiro e o setor produtivo junto aos Estados Unidos. "Essa atuação deve ter uma agenda objetiva de cooperação em controle de exportações, que demonstre a solidez institucional do Brasil e preserve a fluidez das cadeias globais de suprimentos tecnológicos", ressalta a entidade.

artigo.texto: O governo da Bolívia iniciou negociações com o Kawari Fund para estruturar a venda de créditos de carbono provenientes da preservação florestal, transformando a manutenção de ecossistemas em um fluxo de receita financeira direta. O mecanismo, discutido durante a COP31, visa conectar investidores internacionais às comunidades indígenas que atuam na vigilância e proteção dos recursos naturais. A operação baseia-se na iniciativa REDD+ (Redução de Emissões por Desmatamento e Degradação florestal), que atrai capital estrangeiro mediante a comprovação da redução de emissões de gases de efeito estufa. O projeto piloto foi concentrado no Distrito Autônomo Indígena Charua Iyambae, onde a fase atual consiste em consultas obrigatórias para garantir a conformidade dos direitos das comunidades locais antes da implementação do fluxo financeiro. Para viabilizar a atratividade do ativo para os compradores de créditos, o Ministro da Produção Sustentável, Meio Ambiente e Recursos Hídricos, Oscar Mario Justiniano, trabalha na criação de uma estrutura de governança que elimine intermediários. O objetivo é que o pagamento pelos créditos de carbono chegue diretamente ao orçamento das famílias que operam como patrulhas florestais. Segundo Vanessa Jiménez, representante do Kawari Fund, a transparência nos relatórios de destino dos fundos é a condição necessária para que investidores internacionais mantenham o aporte de capital no país. A conversão da floresta em ativo financeiro depende de um processo de verificação técnica, conduzido pela Fundação Amigos da Natureza (FAN) e pela União Internacional para a Conservação da Natureza (CI). Essas entidades são responsáveis pelo monitoramento e a certificação da quantidade de carbono sequestrado, etapa indispensável para que as empresas compradoras possam registrar legalmente as cotas em seus balanços de emissões. Caso o modelo piloto no distrito Charua Iyambae seja validado, a Bolívia pretende expandir a escala da operação, estabelecendo um preço por tonelada de CO2 absorvido que se converta em renda estável para as populações residentes nas áreas florestais. artigo.texto: The Commerce Department on Monday moved to close a loophole that has let Chinese companies lease Nvidia's advanced computing power from data centers in third countries, effectively circumventing controls on sensitive chip technology being exported to China. The interim final rule from Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security is the first U.S. policy response to the scandal that led Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign last week after reports that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who worked for Megaspeed, one of Nvidia's biggest Asian customers. The rule was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and the White House National Security Council, BIS said in a press release. The rule came after growing criticism of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for not doing enough to prevent possible diversion of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China in violation of American export controls. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in an interview on Friday with CNBC's "Squawk Box," blamed the Commerce Department for not putting Singapore-based Megaspeed on its "entity list," which would restrict certain exports to it. Share prices of Nvidia and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence trade fell Monday morning after the interim rule was announced, among them chipmakers Micron Technology, Intel and Advanced Micro Devices. The rule is designed "to prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on U.S. technology to threaten U.S. national security and foreign policy interests," according to the text of the rule. The new restrictions "will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using" advanced artificial intelligence semiconductors produced by U.S. companies to train advanced AI models, the rule says. The rule also says that a license will now "be required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil (and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State or the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs) – countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion." The New York Times reported on Nov. 9 that American authorities began investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed and one of its executives, Alice Huang, in 2024, "after the company started importing billions of dollars' worth of advanced Nvidia A.I. equipment into Malaysia." "Megaspeed had been planning and constructing data centers around Southeast Asia to serve Chinese clients, including Alibaba, the Chinese tech giant," The Times reported that day. "While that behavior is legal, U.S. officials were concerned that some of the Nvidia chips the company had bought were illegally routed into China." Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO last week after reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, and that she was a spy working for China. The two are not related. China's government has denied the claim that Alice Huang was a spy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who, as national security advisor, leads the National Security Council, warned President Donald Trump last spring that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, The Times has reported. Rep. John Mooelnaar, the Michigan Republican who is chairman of the House Select Committee on China, in a statement on the new rule that it "sends a message to the Chinese Communist Party that America is serious about closing dangerous export control loopholes China has been exploiting for years." "Our most advanced AI chips are simply not for sale to our foremost enemy," Moolenaar said. "This new rule is an important step in keeping chips out of ill-intentioned hands, strengthens our national security laws, and will help protect America's lead in the AI race." Chris McGuire, a former deputy senior director for technology and national security at the National Security Council, in a post on X called the new rule "a major step forward to countering Chinese smuggling of and access to advanced AI chips." "The work here is not done, as there are some critical loopholes that remain open and need to be closed in a follow-up rule (namely those related to activities inside the United States)," wrote McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations. "Commerce should move extremely quickly to close these. But this is the first time in over 18 months that the administration is starting to take export controls seriously, and does represent a meaningful step forward." McGuire said that the fact that the new rule was written by and at the direction of the Treasury Department and the NSC "is remarkable and unprecedented." "I have never seen a BIS rule that was not written by BIS," he wrote. "That implies that Commerce was dragged kicking and screaming over the finish line by the White House and Treasury, and instructed to publish this rule rather than the rumored weaker one that it preferred. Remarkable." Commerce's new rule was published a day after Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington state, the ranking Democrat on the Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation, in a letter to Lutnick said that Chinese companies such as Alibaba and ByteDance have "used overseas data centers equipped with advanced Nvidia chips to train advanced AI models." "These companies are exploiting a loophole in U.S. export controls by using advanced American chips in foreign data centers even when those chips are restricted from the [People's Republic of China]," Cantwell wrote. "Despite warnings from the Bureau of Industry and Security that certain arrangements may violate existing restrictions, the Department of Commerce failed to close this loophole, allowing PRC companies to advance their AI capabilities using sensitive American technology," she wrote.

artigo.texto: South Korea's Mplus Wins approximately $15 Million Solid-State Battery Assembly and Electrode Equipment Order from Global Battery Maker Mplus, a South Korean specialist in secondary-battery assembly equipment, has won an order worth approximately 20 billion won (approximately $15.0 million) from a global battery company for assembly and electrode-line equipment used in solid-state battery mass production. According to industry sources on the 16th, the contract covers equipment for the customer's solid-state battery production line, and its significance lies in Mplus securing an official supply track record in the next-generation battery mass-production equipment segment. The equipment to be supplied will use assembly machinery developed in-house by Mplus, incorporating core process technologies such as notching, stacking and precision dispensing. The company is also developing its own roll press technology capable of replacing the warm isostatic press (WIP), which is regarded as a representative pressing process for solid-state batteries. Through this, Mplus aims to build a full lineup of equipment covering all processes required for solid-state battery production. Solid-state batteries are next-generation secondary batteries that replace conventional liquid electrolytes with solid ones. They can improve safety and energy density, but their manufacturing processes are highly demanding, and equipment technology capable of supporting stable mass production is seen as the key to commercialization. As major automakers target the launch of vehicles equipped with solid-state batteries by 2030, battery manufacturers are accelerating facility investment in pilot and mass-production lines. Note: The counterparty and detailed delivery terms were not disclosed. Mplus is also accelerating the diversification of its order portfolio. After recently targeting the multi-purpose specialty battery equipment market, including defense applications, with a European global battery company, it has now also secured this solid-state equipment order, expanding its customer base from a focus on electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems (ESS) into next-generation and specialty battery segments. A company official said, "This order is meaningful in that we have secured an official supply reference in the next-generation solid-state battery mass-production equipment segment," adding, "If the customer's shift to solid-state battery mass production gets into full swing, it could lead to follow-on large orders." The official added, "We also expect additional order opportunities as the customer expands production going forward." Industry observers expect order opportunities for related equipment makers to expand as the solid-state battery market moves beyond the R&D stage into a phase of preparation for commercialization. In particular, they say a track record of supplying initial production lines could serve as a gauge of competitiveness in future mass-production equipment orders. Mplus manufactures assembly equipment — including notching, stacking, tab welding and packaging for pouch-type, prismatic and solid-state batteries — as well as electrode-line facilities. The company is also expanding its new business portfolio, including autonomous mobile robots (AIMRs) and control systems for the physical AI (artificial intelligence) era. This contract remains at the equipment supply stage, so its immediate contribution to earnings may be limited, but it is significant as a bridgehead for securing additional orders when the shift to solid-state battery mass production takes place. Solid-state batteries are still in the early stages of mass production and process standards have not yet been established, so companies that supply equipment for initial lines are seen as potentially holding an advantageous position in subsequent equipment orders. However, some note that with the customer unidentified and the mass-production schedule unconfirmed, whether follow-on orders materialize depends on the pace of the customer's investment execution. artigo.texto: NTT Eyes Space Optical Communications Network, Lunar Power Supply and Space Data Centers NTT President Akira Shimada said in a November 16 lecture in Tokyo that the company will build a space optical communications network linking satellites to each other and to ground communications equipment via optical signals. The company aims to mount electronic components compatible with its next-generation high-speed communications platform IOWN on satellites and other communications devices, creating a system that efficiently delivers satellite-acquired data to ground receiving stations by routing it through another satellite positioned closer to the receiver. Shimada also outlined plans to work on space data centers and power-generation infrastructure on the lunar surface. "NTT will use the technology it has cultivated to weave an optical information network across space," Shimada said, stressing the significance of extending the company's communications control technology into the space domain. Optical communications can transmit far larger volumes of data than radio waves, but are vulnerable to weather and atmospheric conditions, including blockage by clouds. NTT will need technology to accurately transmit data to satellites moving at speeds that circle the Earth in about 90 minutes, as well as the ability to select communications routes that connect multiple satellites and ground equipment along the shortest path. Shimada also said that "the major social roles space will play are communications and observation." Analyzing high-resolution imagery captured by satellites can be used to assess conditions during wildfires and disasters, as well as to survey the distribution of wildlife and vegetation. NTT also anticipates demand for satellite communications as a supplement in mountainous areas and remote islands where terrestrial networks are hard to reach. NTT plans to deploy ground communications equipment around the world by fiscal 2029. Partnership with ispace to study lunar infrastructure NTT announced the same day that it has signed a partnership agreement with space venture ispace (Chuo Ward, Tokyo). The two companies will pursue research, development, demonstration and study toward future commercialization of infrastructure technologies including high-speed optical communications in cislunar space—the region between Earth and the Moon—and wireless laser power transmission on the lunar surface. As lunar exploration advances, a wide variety of data will be generated, including sensor data and activity logs in addition to measurement data. Communications and power infrastructure will be essential to transmit this data to Earth and share it on the Moon as well. From an economic security standpoint, experts have also pointed to the importance of Japan taking the lead in building and managing such infrastructure. While expanding its optical communications research into space, NTT has been developing laser wireless power transmission technology with an eye toward applications beyond communications. ispace, through the lunar landers and rovers its group develops and operates, is working to provide lunar transportation and lunar data services. It plans "Mission 3," targeting a lunar landing in 2028, and aims to commercialize communications and positioning services using lunar orbiters, with plans to launch its first orbiter as early as 2027 under "Mission 2.5." The two companies will combine NTT's optical technologies, including optical communications and laser power transmission, with ispace's expertise in lunar transportation, exploration and mission operations to verify the applicability of optical technology to the lunar environment. Private-sector entry accelerates in U.S.-China-led space race The United States and China are vying for leadership in space development, with countries competing over the number of satellites launched. SpaceX, led by entrepreneur Elon Musk, is pursuing a plan to expand its satellite constellation to 42,000. China has set out a vision of deploying more than 200,000 satellites by the mid-2030s, and South Korea plans to build a network of 7,000 communications satellites. Major IT companies such as Amazon.com are also entering the field, intensifying competition over the use of low-Earth-orbit satellites. The concept of placing computing infrastructure in space is also gaining traction as an alternative to ground-based data centers, which are increasingly struggling to secure power and cooling water. NTT's space data center initiative is seen as aimed at capturing this demand. Market impact For NTT, space optical communications represent an attempt to open a new revenue stream from IOWN-related technology. With Japan's domestic communications market maturing, satellite communications and space infrastructure are drawing attention as areas with significant growth potential. If the partnership with ispace moves from demonstration to commercialization, it could raise the profile of Japanese companies in international competition over lunar transportation and data communications. At the same time, SpaceX and Chinese state-owned enterprises boast overwhelming launch volumes for low-Earth-orbit satellites, and international coordination over the use of frequencies and orbits remains a challenge. Putting an optical communications network into practical use requires the mass deployment of satellites and the buildout of ground equipment, raising questions about the scale of investment required. How NTT's expansion into space contributes to its earnings structure will depend on the progress of demonstrations and the timing of commercialization. artigo.texto: Trina Storage and the Swedish company OX2 signed a framework agreement for the supply of battery energy storage systems (BESS) with an approximate capacity of 3 GWh. The equipment will be used in projects in Finland, Sweden, Poland, and Italy, most of which are expected to become operational by 2028. The agreement is part of OX2 expansion of its European energy storage portfolio and includes standalone installations and hybrid solutions linked to renewable generation projects. According to the planned schedule, the projects will reach financial close between 2026 and 2027. Trina Storage will supply BESS systems in four European countries Trina Storage, Trinasolar’s energy storage division, will provide battery systems for various projects developed by OX2 in the European market. The agreement includes approximately 3 GWh of storage capacity, distributed among facilities located in Finland, Sweden, Poland and Italy. The collaboration will allow progress in the development of a portfolio of projects that combines stand-alone BESS systems with installations integrated into renewable energy plants. Although the companies have not detailed the individual capacity of each project or the economic value of the agreement, OX2 anticipates that most of the facilities will begin operating in 2028, once the financing, construction and commissioning stages are completed. These systems will allow electricity to be stored and supplied later according to the operational needs of the network. Energy storage is gaining importance in Europe The growing incorporation of solar and wind power generation there is a growing need for technologies that bring flexibility to European electricity systems. In this scenario, BESS systems allow energy to be stored for certain periods and supplied when generation or demand conditions require it. Furthermore, they can contribute to the stability of electrical networks through regulation and rapid response services, depending on the technical and commercial characteristics of each installation. For OX2, this technology represents a growth opportunity in both independent projects and hybrid solutions that combine renewable production and storage. Paolo Romanacci, OX2 operations director, highlighted that the company’s storage business continues to grow through both development methods. The executive also expressed his satisfaction at establishing a long-term collaboration with Trina Storage, which will allow progress in the execution of OX2 European project portfolio. OX2 expands its investments in solar energy and batteries in Poland The new collaboration with Trina Storage comes after OX2 announced further investments in renewable generation and energy storage in the Polish market. In June 2026, the company announced investment decisions for two projects, one being the Lion photovoltaic park and the other a battery storage facility in Osiek Jasielski. The Lion solar park, located in the municipality of Sława, in the Lubusz Voivodeship, will have a maximum capacity of 165 MWp and will be one of the largest photovoltaic projects developed by OX2 in Poland. Once operational, it is estimated to produce approximately 184 GWh of electricity per year, a volume equivalent to the annual consumption of about 51,000 homes, according to estimates announced by the company. Furthermore, Osiek Jasielski BESS installation will have a capacity of 50 MW and a storage capacity of 120 MWh. This project represents OX2’s first investment in battery storage in Poland. Both initiatives are part of the company’s expansion in the Polish electricity sector and reflect its interest in combining renewable generation assets with storage technologies. Finland promotes new high-capacity BESS systems Finland has also become a relevant market for OX2 growth in energy storage, in February 2026, the company reached a seven-year agreement with Statkraft for the optimization of two BESS facilities currently under construction. The projects will have a combined capacity of 235 MW and a total energy capacity of 470 MWh. One of the facilities will have 110 MW of power and 220 MWh of storage, while the second will have 125 MW and 250 MWh. Both systems will be located next to the Kannisto wind farm project in Halsua and the Korkeamaa wind farm project in Soini, and are scheduled to become operational in 2028. Under the terms of the agreement, Statkraft will take over the commercial optimization of the batteries, with the aim of managing its participation in the electricity market and taking advantage of the opportunities associated with system flexibility. These investments demonstrate the growth of OX2 storage portfolio in Northern Europe, where BESS systems are becoming increasingly important to complement renewable generation. The 3 GWh agreement reinforces OX2 expansion in Europe The alliance between Trina Storage and OX2 represents a new step in the development of large-scale energy storage projects in Europe. The planned supply of 3 GWh will support a significant part of the Swedish company’s European portfolio, while it moves forward with the financing and execution of new facilities. The financial closings planned between 2026 and 2027 will be crucial to completing the projects included in the agreement. With most of the facilities scheduled to become operational in 2028, the collaboration seeks to expand the availability of storage systems and strengthen the integration of renewable energy into the electricity markets of Finland, Sweden, Poland, and Italy. artigo.texto: Today’s ESG Updates - Data Centers Emitting on the Scale of a Country: A study by a team of Harvard researchers analyzed electricity use at the largest data centers and estimated 28.3 million tons of carbon produced. - Tough Negotiations on Climate Change at COP31: Nearly 200 countries at the conference appear unable to agree on climate mitigation strategies, as the first draft was rejected by some countries the same day. - EU Sets Tariffs on Steel, Mostly From Asia: The EU is imposing tariffs on cold-rolled flat steel products from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey, and Vietnam; the duties take effect Tuesday, November 17. - Proposal to Ease ESG Reporting Rules Met With Disagreement: The European Union faces criticism over a proposal to relax sustainability reporting requirements for companies headquartered outside the bloc. New study shows the true scale of data center emissions Harvard researchers examined 403 of the largest U.S. data centers over a year, between May 2024 and April 2025. The estimated numbers: 28.3 million tons of carbon dioxide and 82 terawatt-hours of electricity from fossil fuels. The first reactions from the expert community agree that the estimate is realistic. Despite claiming that carbon-free power is essential for data centers, former U.S. Vice President and climate activist Al Gore argued that there is hope. In his opinion, advanced AI will eventually help find ways to use energy more efficiently. Another potential upside is the heat coming from data centers; capturing it can provide heat to homes and businesses in the area. The International Energy Agency estimates that by 2030 this can be the heat source for 10% of European homes. Klimado – Navigating climate complexity just got easier. Klimado offers a user-friendly platform for tracking local and global environmental shifts, making it an essential tool for climate-aware individuals and organizations. COP31 heated negotiations reflect the year of heatwaves COP31 negotiators published a draft deal on Monday, with the main gaps between countries including fossil fuels and climate financing. Country representatives need to reach an agreement by the end of this week. Australia’s Chris Bowen, who is leading the negotiation, said some countries have already rejected the latest 18-page draft. The event reflects a year of global warming that caused wildfires in Europe and glacier melting in Nepal. Other crises, like wars and the rising cost of living, limit political motivation. The annual UN climate talks seem unable to reach consensus among almost 200 nations. At the same time, the situation is dire: the latest UN report said the world is on course to exceed the 1.5 °C threshold for the worst climate change effects. Related Articles Here is a list of articles selected by our Editorial Board that have gained significant interest from the public: EU imposes duties on steel to balance prices The new tariffs follow the bloc’s findings that steel products from India, Japan, Taiwan, Turkey, and Vietnam were sold at unfairly low prices. The rates are set at 9.5% for Indian producers, 27.9% for Japanese steelmakers, and up to 20.7% for Taiwanese companies. The total EU market for cold-rolled flat steel is around €23.2 billion, while imports from the now-tariffed countries accounted for about €1.78 billion. Dumping duties like these typically come from comparing producers’ domestic sales prices. However, that applies only to normally functioning markets. For example, the EU uses a normal value for Chinese products outside the country. Here, the European Commission stated that government measures distorted Indian domestic prices. Easing ESG reporting for non-EU companies becomes an unpopular proposal An initiative to ease ESG requirements for companies headquartered outside of the bloc was backed by U.S. business lobbying groups. Naturally, its main aim was to decrease the regulatory burden for international business. The proposal has sparked a dispute around the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), which requires disclosure on environmental, social, and governance impacts. The European Commission suggests a mixed approach for non-EU companies that could potentially narrow their global reporting requirements. According to the proposal, international companies would have more limited requirements on worldwide impacts but would keep the requirements for products and services inside the EU. This suggestion has encountered opposition within the bloc. The main dilemma is maintaining ambitious disclosure standards to protect competitive fairness for European companies. ___________________________________________________________________________________ Editor’s Note: The opinions expressed here by the authors are their own, not those of impakter.com — Cover Photo Credit: Chad Davis

artigo.texto: Data centers: acordo entre Amazon e Blackstone abrange 13 prédios em Indiana e no Mississippi (Adobe Stock/Divulgação) Repórter de Inteligência Artificial e Tecnologia Publicado em 16 de novembro de 2026 às 10h10. Última atualização em 16 de novembro de 2026 às 10h11. A Amazon anunciou em 16 de novembro de 2026 a venda do controle de 13 prédios de data centers nos Estados Unidos, avaliados em US$ 5 bilhões, para a Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC), veículo imobiliário administrado por uma afiliada da Blackstone. A Amazon Web Services (AWS) continuará ocupando todos os imóveis como inquilina, com contratos de prazo médio inicial de 12 anos, que podem chegar a 32 anos com as renovações, e reajuste de 2,75% ao ano. A Amazon receberá dinheiro e ficará com 24,9% das duas sociedades conjuntas que serão donas dos complexos, localizados em Indiana e no Mississippi, que somam 647 megawatts de capacidade. É o primeiro investimento da BXDC desde o IPO, em maio, e a conclusão está prevista para até o fim de 2026. O modelo lembra a sociedade fechada pela Meta com fundos da Blue Owl, em 2025, para o complexo Hyperion, na Louisiana. A Amazon vai passar de proprietária a sócia minoritária e inquilina de 13 prédios de data centers recém-construídos nos Estados Unidos. Em acordo anunciado nesta segunda-feira, 16, um veículo imobiliário administrado por uma afiliada da Blackstone comprará o controle das sociedades que ficarão com os imóveis, avaliados em US$ 5 bilhões. A Amazon Web Services (AWS), braço de computação em nuvem do grupo, vai alugar todos os prédios e continuar usando a infraestrutura. A operação dá à Amazon uma forma de levantar dinheiro com instalações que já construiu e manter a capacidade disponível para seus clientes. Em troca, a companhia assume aluguéis com prazo inicial médio de 12 anos. Se todas as opções de renovação forem exercidas, a média sobe para 32 anos. O reajuste previsto é de 2,75% ao ano, e a própria Amazon garante os pagamentos da subsidiária. Os US$ 5 bilhões correspondem à avaliação bruta dos dois complexos. Na conclusão da operação, a Amazon vai transferir os imóveis para duas sociedades conjuntas, uma para cada complexo, e receber dinheiro e uma fatia de 24,9% em cada uma. A Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, negociada na Bolsa de Nova York sob o código BXDC, ficará com os outros 75,1%. O pagamento em dinheiro será financiado por duas fontes. A BXDC espera aportar US$ 1,9 bilhão em recursos levantados no IPO. Subsidiárias das sociedades conjuntas devem contratar cerca de US$ 2,5 bilhões em empréstimos hipotecários, garantidos pelos próprios imóveis. Como parte do financiamento também cobrirá custos da transação, a soma dessas duas fontes indica o volume de recursos mobilizados, e o valor líquido a ser recebido pela Amazon ainda depende dos termos do fechamento. É o primeiro investimento da BXDC desde a abertura de capital, em maio. A oferta inicial foi de US$ 1,75 bilhão e, depois que os bancos exerceram integralmente a opção de vender ações adicionais, a captação líquida chegou a cerca de US$ 1,9 bilhão. A conclusão da compra está prevista para até o fim de 2026, sujeita às condições do acordo. O acordo reúne nove prédios no norte de Indiana, no mercado de data centers da região de Chicago, e quatro no Mississippi. Juntos, eles somam 647 megawatts de capacidade elétrica para equipamentos de TI. O número indica a potência que a infraestrutura pode disponibilizar a equipamentos como servidores e sistemas de rede. Para a BXDC, a compra dá acesso a prédios novos com um contrato para ocupar 100% do portfólio. Para a AWS, a locação mantém disponíveis os imóveis de que a operação depende. O contrato segue o modelo conhecido como triple net, em que o inquilino arca, além do aluguel, com despesas como impostos imobiliários, seguro e manutenção. A aquisição foi precificada a uma taxa inicial de capitalização de 7%. O indicador relaciona a renda operacional anual dos imóveis ao valor atribuído a eles. Ele serve para avaliar o preço pago pelo portfólio. O retorno para o acionista da BXDC também depende do custo da dívida e das demais despesas da operação. A parceria permite à Amazon recuperar parte do capital investido nas instalações e continuar usando os prédios. O dinheiro entra no fechamento. Os aluguéis serão pagos ao longo dos anos, com reajuste anual. Para o investidor imobiliário, o atrativo é justamente o fluxo de pagamentos de uma única locatária, respaldado pela garantia da Amazon. Prasad Kalyanaraman, vice-presidente de infraestrutura da AWS, afirmou no comunicado que a parceria permite à empresa continuar ampliando sua operação à medida que cresce a demanda dos clientes. No terceiro trimestre, a receita da AWS cresceu 39%, para US$ 46 bilhões. A expansão exige investimentos em terrenos, energia e prédios, além dos chips e servidores instalados neles. O acordo com a Blackstone traz um investidor para a parte imobiliária dessa conta. A Meta recorreu a uma sociedade com fundos da Blue Owl em outubro de 2025 para desenvolver o complexo Hyperion, na Louisiana. Os fundos ficaram com 80%, e a Meta, com 20%. Os US$ 27 bilhões divulgados naquele acordo correspondem ao custo estimado de desenvolvimento, incluindo construção e infraestrutura de energia, refrigeração e conectividade. No caso da Amazon, os US$ 5 bilhões são a avaliação de imóveis já construídos, que a AWS continuará usando como inquilina. A AWS vai alugar todos os 13 prédios. A Amazon também manterá 24,9% das sociedades que serão donas dos imóveis. Os US$ 5 bilhões são o valor bruto atribuído aos dois complexos. Na conclusão do negócio, a Amazon receberá uma parcela em dinheiro e manterá uma participação minoritária nas sociedades. A BXDC espera concluir a transação até o fim de 2026. O fechamento depende das condições do acordo e do financiamento previsto.
