artigo.texto: Industrial Manufacturing Norway Halts Data Center Projects as AI Booms Norway says stoppage is necessary to ensure 'proper operation' of the power system Released Monday, November 16, 2026 Written by Martin Lynch, European News Editor for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary As global AI data center growth accelerates, Norway has opted to press pause on related grid connection applications in an effort to regulate the kinds of data centers it wants built in the future. Stemming the AI Boom Norway's government has introduced a halt to grid connection applications for data center projects in an attempt to regulate the growing demands on its power grid. Statnett, the national grid operator, has introduced a "temporary suspension of further reservation of network capacity for data centers" and claimed the stoppage is necessary to ensure "proper operation" of the power system. It said it wants to ensure a "controlled growth of data centers in Norway and that they are as beneficial to society as possible". The government is now working on a number of measures and aims to introduce a licensing scheme for data centers in the coming year. The ban could stay in place until August 2027. According to Industrial Info Resources data, there are 74 active data center projects planned worth more than US$39 billion in investment. The Global Market Intelligence (GMI) Industrial Manufacturing Project Database offers a list of detailed project reports. The Government Take "We are facilitating more and faster development of power and networks, but it is neither desirable nor possible to develop enough to cover the power demand that comes from data centers that want to establish themselves in Norway," said Minister of Energy Terje Aasland. "We must have enough power in the right place for socially beneficial purposes. That is why we are taking action now." Torgeir Micaelsen, minister of digitalization and public administration, added: "Data centers are part of our critical infrastructure. They contribute to value creation, secure digital services and greater digital independence for Norway. But we have been clear that we do not want all types of data centers in Norway. We need those that contribute the most social benefit. Therefore, the government is starting work on a licensing scheme that will set requirements and conditions for the establishment and operation of data centers." The Problem According to Statnett, it has so far this year received applications for around 26,000 megawatts (MW) of new consumption in Norway, with data centers accounting for three quarters of those requests. Aasland said: "That's more than all of Norway's consumption today." Statnett said that today, data centers with a total power consumption of 800 MW have been connected to the grid, 4,200 MW have been reserved grid capacity and 9,100 MW are in the capacity queue. In addition, there are requests for connection of a further 18,000 MW. In comparison, the maximum power consumption in Norway is just over 25,000 MW. Norwegian data centers used 3.2 terawatt hours (TWh) of electricity last year according to a report from Menon Economics last month. That's four times more than three years ago. Proposed Measures - Licensing: The first step the government will take is to introduce a licensing scheme for establishing and operating data centers in Norway. Micaelsen said that priority in licensing will be given to data centers serving defense, police, emergency response services, healthcare services and other critical infrastructure, including mobile networks and the financial system. Norway will restrict access to land and electricity for global cloud companies and cryptocurrency businesses. Data centers that conduct crypto business will not be considered socially beneficial, according to the government. - Digital security and preparedness: Requirements and conditions that support digital security and preparedness, as well as contribute to the necessary AI computing power in Norway, the Nordic region and Europe, will be considered. - Modernize the connection obligation: The government will modernize the regulations that oblige network companies to connect consumption to the electricity grid, so that it is better adapted to the actual situation where the grid queue far exceeds what is possible to handle. - Get more of the costs covered: The government wants large new power consumers to contribute more to covering the costs of developing a new grid and costs incurred in system operation. It is assessing whether a distinction can be made between new large consumption and large expansion of existing consumption. - New contributions to power production: The government will talk to the data center industry about how it can help build new power sources to deal with increased demand using gas-fired power plants with carbon capture and storage, and offshore wind. - Consider state ownership: The government will investigate different models for state ownership in data center projects of particular societal benefit. Unhappy Industry Reaction The Norwegian Data Center Industry (NDI) has reacted by claiming the move by the government and Statnett will create uncertainty for billions of dollars in investment. "Billions of kroner are invested every month in Norwegian data centers, with most of it going to the supplier industry," said NDI Chief Executive Officer Reynir Johannesson. "This is about construction workers, electricians and engineers all over the country. They deserve to know what rules apply in both the short and long term." He added: "The government uses the electricity queue as a justification, but does not launch a single measure that clears the queue. Poland cut its queue by 90% in a few months earlier this year by requiring applicants to put money on the table. artigo.texto: Durham has just 75 days of easily accessible water remaining if no rain falls, and Falls Lake has dropped to its lowest level since the drought crisis of 2007. As water supplies dwindle across the Triangle, some residents are pointing the finger at a rapidly growing industry: data centers. Other WRAL Top Stories Comments on recent WRAL social media posts about the drought have raised concerns about the facilities consuming large amounts of drinking water. But water consumption figures provided by Raleigh and Durham show that other customers account for much more of the cities' water demand. Drought is caused by a lack of precipitation, but water consumption can determine how long communities' supplies last. How much water do Durham's data centers use? Durham officials have identified six customers with facilities that could be classified as data centers. Four of those facilities collectively consume approximately 1.88 million gallons of water per month, accounting for just 0.2% of the city's overall water use. At the other two facilities, officials cannot distinguish water used to cool data centers from water used for other purposes. Data center water consumption also tends to increase during the hotter summer months, according to the city. Residential customers account for the largest share of Durham's water demand: - Residential: 52% - Commercial and industrial: 36.6% - Institutional, including schools and places of worship: 11.4% Durham estimates it has 145 days of total water supply remaining, including 75 days of easily accessible water. Those projections are based on a 30-day running average of demand on the city's reservoirs and assume no rainfall. Who uses the most water in Raleigh? In Raleigh, nearly two-thirds of water demand comes from residential customers. Just 4% goes to the entire industrial category. Raleigh Water official Ed Buchan said the utility serves a handful of traditional data centers, including facilities that handle banking information, but no large-scale generative AI data centers. “But we don't really have any significant demand from industrial customers, and certainly none from generative AI,” Buchan said. “So that is not an issue in our service area.” Despite the Triangle's rapid population growth, Raleigh's water demand has increased relatively modestly over the past two decades. In 2007, Raleigh Water's average demand was 52 million gallons per day. Today, it's about 60 million gallons per day, including water supplied to additional wholesale customers. Buchan attributes that trend in part to more efficient household appliances and conservation habits that developed during the previous drought crisis. One of the biggest drivers of additional water demand during the summer is lawn irrigation, which can account for 17 million to 18 million gallons of water per day. Not all data centers use the same amount of water Water consumption can vary significantly depending on how a data center is designed and cooled. Cooling towers and evaporative cooling systems can consume large amounts of water, while closed-loop systems and air cooling can substantially reduce water consumption. Durham officials said a proposed data center in Research Triangle Park would use city water for standard office needs but not for cooling. Instead, the facility has proposed using reclaimed water from Durham County. Officials also said data centers would be subject to the same drought-related water restrictions as other customers. Can North Carolina handle future data center demand? In Richmond County, where Amazon Web Services is developing a massive data center campus, economic development officials say they evaluated the project's water needs alongside engineers and public works staff. “We're not having to expand our water treatment plant,” a Richmond County economic development official told WRAL earlier this year. “We have plenty of capacity to supply AWS at peak buildout in the hottest days of the summer.” Amazon is also funding water distribution infrastructure upgrades needed to serve the campus, according to county officials. Those assessments are based on projected demand, rather than actual water consumption from a fully operational campus. In the Triangle, both Raleigh and Durham have temporarily paused approvals for certain new data center developments as they consider regulations for future projects. Raleigh's moratorium lasts six months, while Durham's lasts nine months. Buchan said Raleigh Water has contacted utilities across the country that already serve large data centers to learn how they manage the industry's water demand. While the available figures do not indicate that data centers are a major driver of current water demand in Raleigh or Durham, the industry's rapid expansion raises a longer-term question: how much additional demand can North Carolina's water systems handle, particularly during prolonged drought? Water officials urge conservation Raleigh Water is encouraging customers to conserve water even though mandatory restrictions have not been implemented. Buchan recommends reducing lawn irrigation, taking shorter showers and checking homes for leaks. “That said, the whole region is clearly in a very serious drought situation,” Buchan said. “So we would ask our customers and anybody listening to this to try to conserve water, no matter where you're at.”

artigo.texto: Na Cúpula do Clima das Nações Unidas COP31, em Antalya, Turquia, o Vietnã lançou oficialmente o portal público CarbonVN. Este evento marca um ponto de virada na infraestrutura digital, ajudando o mercado de carbono doméstico a acelerar a integração e a antecipar os fluxos globais de financiamento climático. Segundo informações do PNUD Vietnam, o portal de informações públicas CarbonVN foi desenvolvido sob os auspícios do Ministério da Agricultura e Meio Ambiente , implementado diretamente pelo Departamento de Mudanças Climáticas (DCC) com o apoio do PNUD. Esta plataforma permite que empresas, investidores, instituições financeiras e cidadãos acessem facilmente dados sobre cotas de emissão, créditos de carbono, listas de projetos registrados e políticas relacionadas. O Vietnã lançou o portal de informações públicas CarbonVN na COP31, fornecendo cotas de carbono transparentes e dados de mercado para investidores (Foto: PNUD Vietnã). Os sistemas de informação pública e os sistemas nacionais de registo constituem a infraestrutura digital essencial. Para os investidores financeiros, a transparência e a rastreabilidade dos dados são pré-requisitos para a avaliação de ativos e o investimento. Essa iniciativa coincide com o lançamento, pelo Vietnã, de uma plataforma piloto de negociação de carbono na Bolsa de Valores de Hanói (HNX), um passo rumo à meta de emissões líquidas zero até 2050. A digitalização de todos os dados de transações e cotas ajuda a suprir a lacuna de informações, aumentando a confiança das instituições financeiras internacionais que buscam projetos de redução de emissões no Vietnã. A onda de conectividade global e a oportunidade para fluxos de investimento de bilhões de dólares. Paralelamente ao progresso do Vietnã, na COP31, a Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Comércio e Desenvolvimento (UNCTAD) lançou oficialmente a Rede Global do Mercado de Carbono. Essa iniciativa reúne importantes bolsas de valores, bancos e instituições financeiras internacionais, como a Climate Impact X ( Singapura ), a Bolsa de Valores da Indonésia, a Verra e o Conselho de Desenvolvimento de Serviços Financeiros de Hong Kong (China). Segundo a UNCTAD, os mecanismos de precificação de carbono estão se expandindo rapidamente em todo o mundo. Os sistemas de comércio de emissões (SCE) e os impostos sobre o carbono agora abrangem quase 30% das emissões globais, gerando mais de US$ 107 bilhões em receita pública até 2025. A maioria dos créditos de carbono voluntários gerados atualmente é fornecida por países em desenvolvimento a compradores em países desenvolvidos. Ao comentar sobre o papel do mercado, Nan Li Collins, Diretora de Investimento e Empreendedorismo da UNCTAD e Presidente da Iniciativa das Nações Unidas para Bolsas de Valores Sustentáveis, enfatizou que os mercados de carbono podem contribuir para a precificação das emissões e para a mobilização de financiamento para atividades de resposta às mudanças climáticas. No entanto, a eficácia do mercado depende de confiança, integridade e uma infraestrutura de mercado que funcione de forma eficiente. A rede da UNCTAD concentra-se na padronização de tecnologias digitais , medição e verificação para minimizar os custos de transações transfronteiriças. A sincronização da infraestrutura digital CarbonVN do Vietname com os padrões internacionais oferece aos projetos verdes nacionais uma oportunidade significativa de acesso a uma rede global de compradores. As instalações de produção industrial estão intensificando a redução de emissões para aproveitar as oportunidades do mercado internacional de créditos de carbono (Foto: MASI). Antecipando mecanismos internacionais e fluxos de financiamento verde. De acordo com o Relatório de Políticas sobre Precificação de Carbono, o quadro legal do Vietnã abriu importantes vias para atrair investimentos internacionais. O Decreto 112/2026/ND-CP estabeleceu três métodos para a transferência de resultados de redução de emissões para o exterior, em conformidade com o Artigo 6º do Acordo de Paris e com padrões independentes. Em nível bilateral, o Vietnã assinou um acordo de implementação nos termos do Artigo 6.2 com Singapura e um Memorando de Cooperação sobre o Mecanismo Conjunto de Crédito (JCM) com o Japão, além de conduzir negociações com a Coreia do Sul e a Suíça . Esses acordos permitem a transferência dos resultados de redução de emissões licenciados e a implementação dos mecanismos de ajuste correspondentes. Juntamente com o mercado de crédito, os fluxos de crédito verde doméstico estão ganhando uma base mais sólida graças à Decisão 21/2025 sobre a lista de classificação verde, que inclui 45 tipos de projetos em 7 setores. Com a verificação transparente dos dados de emissões por meio do Portal CarbonVN, as empresas que reduzem efetivamente as emissões terão uma vantagem significativa no acesso a crédito verde e na emissão de títulos verdes. A infraestrutura transparente da CarbonVN, combinada com os mecanismos de cooperação internacional previstos no Artigo 6, está gradualmente transformando a redução de emissões em recursos financeiros concretos. Este é um pré-requisito fundamental para que o Vietnã avance para a fase operacional de um mercado formal de carbono com leilões até 2029, trazendo gradualmente capital verde global diretamente para projetos nacionais de transição energética e tecnologias de baixo carbono.

artigo.texto: A Moura, marca que os brasileiros conhecem das baterias de partida de carro, vai aplicar R$ 200 milhões numa operação que estoca eletricidade e a devolve ao sistema elétrico. O aporte, segundo a Exame, vai para o complexo industrial de Belo Jardim, no Agreste de Pernambuco. O investimento prepara a companhia para fornecer equipamentos aos projetos que disputarão o primeiro leilão brasileiro dedicado ao armazenamento de energia em baterias. A capacidade de fornecimento anunciada passa de 8 GWh em sistemas BESS, sigla em inglês de battery energy storage system. O equipamento carrega energia nas horas de sobra e devolve a eletricidade à rede quando o consumo aperta. Segundo a Exame, a chinesa CATL aporta a tecnologia, enquanto a Moura responde pela industrialização e pela integração local dos sistemas. No caso das baterias, a CATL assume a venda dos sistemas, por acumular experiência em disputas de leilões em diversos países, incluindo a América Latina. Os detalhes da sociedade foram dados por Spartacus Pedrosa, diretor de operações de lítio do grupo, segundo a Exame. A aliança com a CATL não começa agora e se estende a outras áreas, como a eletrificação de veículos. O investimento já está em execução e inclui obras, linha nova de produção, transferência de tecnologia e formação de profissionais. O valor inclui uma expansão recente da fábrica e um novo ciclo de ampliação, conforme o Movimento Econômico. A empresa, que atua há décadas com tecnologias de acumulação de energia, começou a desenvolver o BESS em meados da década de 2010. O primeiro sistema próprio, o Moura BESS, foi apresentado em 2019 e é produzido em Belo Jardim. O movimento abre uma nova frente para um grupo que registrou receita líquida de R$ 5,04 bilhões em 2025. A estratégia é levar o conhecimento acumulado em baterias para mercados que vão de pequenos negócios à infraestrutura elétrica nacional. Elisa Correia, diretora-presidente da Rede Moura, disse à Exame que a empresa cresceu em ritmo chinês nos últimos anos. Segundo ela, os negócios fora do segmento automotivo têm avançado mais rapidamente, enquanto a empresa já ocupa posição consolidada nas baterias para carros. Os dois falaram à Exame no Recife, durante o REC’n’Play, festival de tecnologia, inovação e negócios.

artigo.texto: HiTHIUM Partners with the University of Cambridge to Advance International Industry-Academia Collaboration in Long-Duration Energy Storage XIAMEN, China, Nov. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On November 12, the Global Energy Storage Colloquium was held in Xiamen. During the colloquium, HiTHIUM and the University of Cambridge signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU), establishing a strategic partnership. The two parties will collaborate on frontier scientific research, key technology innovation and industrial applications in battery energy storage, bringing academic research into closer alignment with industry needs and exploring new models for international industry-academia collaboration. The partnership aims to contribute to the advancement of global energy storage technology and the industry. The UK has a strong track record in the development of modern battery technologies and fundamental research. The University of Cambridge is one of the world's leading universities, with internationally recognized expertise in engineering, materials science and fundamental research. As a leading global energy storage technology company, HiTHIUM has long focused on energy storage technology development and commercialization. It continues to advance integrated research and innovation across the value chain, from high-capacity energy storage cells to long-duration energy storage systems and grid integration technologies. The collaboration is intended to bring internationally leading academic research into closer engagement with innovation across China's energy storage industry. The University of Cambridge's strengths in fundamental science, materials research and engineering will offer new perspectives and approaches to key scientific questions and emerging technologies in energy storage. HiTHIUM will bring its experience in long-duration energy storage (LDES), product development and large-scale deployment, connecting research with real industry needs and application scenarios, and supporting the engineering validation and commercialization of research outcomes. By drawing on the strengths of both research and industry, the partnership will strengthen the links between frontier innovation and practical applications. Under the cooperation plan, the two parties will establish joint management and research collaboration mechanisms, bringing together academic resources and corporate R&D capabilities. They will work together to plan research projects, facilitate scientific exchange and support the translation of research outcomes, strengthening connections between fundamental research, technology development and industrial applications so that innovation in energy storage can better serve industry needs. The partnership also marks an important step in HiTHIUM's efforts to expand its international innovation network. Building on this collaboration with the University of Cambridge, HiTHIUM will further strengthen academic exchanges and research partnerships with leading universities and research institutions around the world. By bringing together international research resources and talent, the company aims to encourage collaboration across disciplines and technology fields, explore the development of technologies such as LDES from a global perspective, and bring technical challenges and application needs from the front lines of industry into research and innovation. This will help research and industrial practice reinforce one another.

artigo.texto: EUA impõem restrição ao Brasil em compras de chips para data centers O governo dos Estado Unidos incluiu o Brasil na lista dos países que enfrentarão restrições para importar chips fabricados no país norte-americano para data centers. Com a decisãodo Escritório de Indústria e Segurança do Departamento de Comércio dos Estados Unidos (BIS, na sigla em Inglês), fornecedores brasileiros precisarão de autorização do governo de Donald Trump para enviar os processadores avançados a empresas brasileiras, com pedidos analisados caso a caso. Segundo o Departamento de Comércio, a norma visa garantir que as restrições existentes ao acesso a tecnologias americanas sensíveis não possam ser contornadas por meio de acordos de computação remota que envolvam centros de dados em países terceiros. Além do Brasil, a restrição inclui Singapura, Tailândia, Malásia e Indonésia, que, segundo a norma, apresentam risco acima do normal de desvio ilegal desses chips para China ou Macau —alvos de embargos junto com Rússia, Irã, Coreia do Norte, Síria e Cuba. Norma norte-americana exige que empresas dos países restringidos solicitem licenças de exportação dos EUA para os chips mais avançados, em um esforço para reduzir o contrabando desses produtos. A proposta dos EUA aborda o cenário tecnológico em evolução. “Alinhando ainda mais as proteções que regem o acesso remoto a recursos computacionais avançados com os controles existentes sobre o transporte físico de tecnologia americana sensível”, disse o Departamento de Comércio. continue lendo - O que se sabe sobre a reunião para a 'paz mundial' que reunirá Trump, Xi e Putin AFP · há 1 hora - Justiça ordena transferência de Peña a prisão militar após denúncias de privilégios Estadão Conteúdo · há 2 horas - Alliana diz que pagamento a aposentados do Ueno Bank acontecerá nesta semana AFP · há 3 horas - Rascunho da COP31 defende acelerar o fim do uso dos combustíveis fósseis AFP · há 6 horas

artigo.texto: Regional carbon market leaders gather for the ASEAN Common Carbon Framework (ACCF) collaboration at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, with the Philippines joining as an Observer through Aboitiz Foundation, representing the CarbonPH Coalition and the Philippines Nature-based Solutions (NbS) Group. From left: Steven Marcelino, Deputy Chair for International Affairs, ASEAN Alliance on Carbon Markets; Oi-Yee Choo, ACCF Co-Chair and CEO of Climate Impact X; Dr. Renard Siew, President of the Malaysia Carbon Market Association; Khun Gloyta Nathalang, Chair of the Thailand Carbon Markets Club; and Faiha Azka Azzahira, Vice Head of Community Development, Indonesia Carbon Trade Association. The Philippines is strengthening its participation in Southeast Asia’s emerging carbon markets through private-sector engagement with the ASEAN Common Carbon Framework (ACCF), contributing to regional efforts to promote carbon market integrity, cooperation, and climate finance. Aboitiz Foundation, representing the CarbonPH Coalition and the Philippines Nature-based Solutions (NbS) Group, is joining the ACCF as an Observer and participating in the signing of its Memorandum of Collaboration (MoC) at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye. The engagement provides an opportunity to bring Philippine perspectives and experience to regional discussions on carbon market standards, financing, and cross-border cooperation. It also highlights the growing role of Philippine private-sector initiatives in advancing forest restoration, nature-based climate solutions, and sustainable investment opportunities. The signing coincides with the renewal of the ACCF’s Memorandum of Collaboration for another two years, reaffirming regional commitments to developing connected, transparent, and high-integrity carbon markets across ASEAN. “ASEAN has the natural capital and economic dynamism to become a significant player in global carbon markets. Through the CarbonPH Coalition and our work in nature-based solutions, we hope to contribute Philippine perspectives and practical experience to this regional effort,” said Ginggay Hontiveros-Malvar, Aboitiz Chief Reputation and Sustainability Officer and President of Aboitiz Foundation. “Our aim is to help build a carbon market where integrity attracts investment, climate action creates economic opportunity, and communities share in the value being created,” she added. The Philippines’ participation builds on ongoing private-sector efforts to strengthen the country’s emerging carbon market ecosystem through industry collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and capacity building. Among these initiatives is the CarbonPH Coalition, which brings together stakeholders to explore opportunities for credible carbon market development and nature-based climate solutions. Complementing these efforts, both CarbonPH Coalition and NbS Group have a long-term nature-based solutions initiative focused on forest restoration, biodiversity conservation, watershed protection, community development and recommended governance frameworks. These efforts highlight the Philippines’ potential to develop nature-based carbon projects that support environmental protection, attract climate financing, and create economic opportunities for local communities. They also provide practical experience that Philippine stakeholders can bring to regional discussions as ASEAN works toward a more connected and credible carbon market. Established in 2024, the ACCF brings together carbon market organizations from Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Thailand, alongside the ASEAN Alliance on Carbon Markets, to strengthen regional coordination and advance the development of high-integrity carbon markets. Under its 2026–2028 strategy, the framework is prioritizing broader ASEAN representation, alignment with international standards, stronger market infrastructure, and technical cooperation to support credible carbon financing and cross-border market development. This representation creates an avenue for Philippine private-sector stakeholders to contribute local perspectives, share practical experience, and learn from regional carbon market initiatives. For the Philippines, the engagement marks another opportunity to strengthen regional partnerships, support the development of credible carbon market mechanisms, and attract investment in climate solutions that benefit both the environment and local communities.As ASEAN advances cooperation on carbon markets, Philippine private-sector participation can help connect regional climate financing opportunities with local conservation efforts, sustainable livelihoods, and long-term environmental resilience.

artigo.texto: This high-tech Huawei home battery pack hopes to hold back Tesla’s latest Powerwall with silicon carbide technology, AI-powered energy management baked in, and enough modular storage to keep even large homes bright and warm when the rest of the block goes dark. Huawei believes its new Luterra S2 is more than just a home backup battery. The Chinese tech firm is calling it an “all-in-one residential energy system” that combines a hybrid inverter, modular battery storage, and AI-powered energy management in a single, simple, and stackable package that’s available in single-phase versions that put out between 3 and 10 kW and three-phase versions that can push up to 20 kW. The Luterra S2 is the first system of its kind to use Huawei’s proprietary full-silicon carbide (SiC) architecture, which promises improved efficiency, power density, and ease of use. It’s so easy, in fact, that Huawei claims it can be installed and commissioned in just minutes. “We are thrilled to introduce Huawei Luterra S2, our next-generation all-in-one residential energy system,” said Steve Zhang, President of Huawei Distributed PV & BESS Business. “By combining full-SiC architecture, AI-driven energy management, and industry-leading safety, Luterra S2 is designed to be smaller, lighter, quieter, safer, smarter and more powerful than ever before.” All about the all in one Huawei’s basic Luterra S2 configuration starts with “just” 5 kWh of battery energy storage and 3 kW of output. That’s enough to keep essential household appliances, lighting, and electronics running during a power outage, but you’ll want to keep going if you’re preparing for more than a day or two without power. If that sounds like you, Luterra’s got you covered. The modular system can be expanded with modular 7 kWh LFP battery packs and can scaling up to a massive 336 kWh of total storage across interconnected systems, with inverter output peaking at an impressive 60 kW using three 20 kW units in parallel. Keeping all that power cool and quiet is a Huawei-developed passive cooling system that does without external fans, keeping operating noise levels below a claimed 29 dB (about the same as my Mac mini). It operates at ambient temperatures from –25° C to about 60° C, and features a sturdy IP66-rated enclosure (safe to hit with a high-pressure hose) with corrosion protection up to C5-M to keep it from rusting away. Alas, the Luterra S2 probably won’t be making its way to the US anytime soon – but fear not! artigo.texto: Malta Maritime Forum calls for a fairer emissions trading system Prime minister's arguments at EU summit lauded Malta Maritime Forum calls for a fairer system and backs the Prime Minister’s stand in the national interest. The Malta Maritime Forum (MMF) has welcomed the 'firm position' taken by the prime minister at the recent European Political Community meeting in Ireland, where, it said, he echoed the MMF’s criticism of the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS). The MMF views the ETS as harming Europe and Malta, and must be changed. "The ETS was poorly designed. It was passed in record time, without a proper, broad consultation process with the maritime industry. The result is an impractical system that created unfair competition for European ports," it said. "The ETS is not delivering the climate results it promised. The EU cannot apply its laws outside its own territory. As a result, Europe is losing business, investment and maritime connectivity to North Africa, where the ETS applies differently or may not apply at all," it explained. " Whilst shipping routes are increasingly diverting southwards, emissions are not falling; they are simply moving elsewhere, together with the jobs and investment that go with them." Robert Abela made the same point at the summit meeting, saying the EU is shooting itself in the foot with ETS. The impact of ETS is disproportionate on Malta relative to other Member States because it has no alternatives such as rail or inland waterways to keep goods moving, and it is the most open economy in the EU27. The MMF said it is ready to continue working with the government on fair and practical solutions and to present them to the EU with a unified national voice. One key proposal is to apply the ETS to the cargo, whether containerised or not, rather than to the vessel carrying it. " Any solution must ensure a level playing field and avoid putting EU ports and shipping services at an unfair disadvantage," it stressed. artigo.texto: GCC e EXIST assinam acordo de cooperação para o mercado de carbono na COP31 O Global Carbon Council e a bolsa de energia da Turquia, Enerji Piyasalari Isletme A.S., conhecida internacionalmente como Energy Exchange Istanbul (EXIST), assinaram um Memorando de Entendimento para aprofundar a cooperação no desenvolvimento do mercado de carbono e examinar a negociação de créditos de carbono emitidos pelo GCC na Turquia, segundo a QNA. O acordo foi assinado no Pavilhão Climático Árabe, organizado conjuntamente pelo GCC e pela Liga dos Estados Árabes, durante a 31ª Conferência das Nações Unidas sobre Mudanças Climáticas, em Antália, na Turquia. O memorando foi assinado pelo Dr. Yousef Alhorr, presidente fundador do GCC, e por Taha Meli Arvas, CEO e vice-presidente do Conselho de Administração da EPIAS. A cooperação tem como objetivo facilitar o uso do programa de certificação de carbono do GCC, reconhecido internacionalmente, na Turquia, abrir novos caminhos para que os participantes do mercado acessem créditos de carbono de alta integridade e reforçar a capacidade técnica à medida que o país constrói seu marco regulatório de mercado de carbono. Unir expertise em padrões à operação de mercados O arranjo combina a experiência do GCC em padrões de certificação de carbono, registro de projetos e emissão de créditos com a expertise da EPIAS na operação de mercados organizados de energia e ambientais. O objetivo é apoiar mecanismos de mercado transparentes que conectem projetos confiáveis de redução de emissões a compradores e investidores, contribuindo ao mesmo tempo para as estratégias climáticas corporativas e para os objetivos climáticos nacionais. Nos termos do memorando, as duas organizações vão explorar a listagem e a negociação dos Créditos de Carbono Aprovados do GCC nas plataformas de negociação da EPIAS, sujeitas às regulamentações e aos requisitos de mercado aplicáveis. Também vão examinar se os créditos poderiam ser reconhecidos no futuro marco regulatório de mercado de carbono regulado da Turquia. A cooperação proposta poderia ampliar o acesso ao mercado para desenvolvedores de projetos e compradores e incentivar o registro, a emissão e o uso de créditos de carbono de alta qualidade por meio de processos de negociação transparentes. Capacitação e apoio técnico Além da negociação, o acordo enfatiza a capacitação e o intercâmbio de conhecimento. O GCC e a EPIAS pretendem realizar workshops, webinars, seminários e outras atividades para melhorar a compreensão dos requisitos do mercado de carbono entre potenciais participantes e partes interessadas locais. O GCC também apoiará o acesso a informações disponíveis publicamente sobre seu programa de certificação, seu registro e suas metodologias. A cooperação poderá contar com a expertise da Gulf Organisation for Research and Development, organização-mãe do GCC, para apoiar a preparação do mercado e o desenvolvimento de capacidade técnica na Turquia. Entre as possíveis áreas de apoio estão o treinamento em contabilidade de gases de efeito estufa, monitoramento, relato e verificação, requisitos de ajuste de carbono na fronteira e divulgação de sustentabilidade segundo os Padrões Turcos de Relato de Sustentabilidade, alinhados às normas IFRS S1 e S2. As partes também poderão explorar a aplicação de soluções digitais da GORD, incluindo a SustainoAI, para contabilidade de gases de efeito estufa, relatos ESG e cálculos de emissões financiadas, além de assistência técnica mais ampla em descarbonização e eficiência energética. Posições dos signatários O Dr. Alhorr comentou que mercados de carbono confiáveis dependem da conexão entre créditos de alta integridade e uma infraestrutura de mercado transparente e bem estruturada, e que a cooperação com a EPIAS cria uma oportunidade de fortalecer essas conexões na Turquia, ao mesmo tempo que apoia o conhecimento e a capacidade institucional de que os mercados precisam para crescer de forma responsável. Ele indicou que um objetivo mais amplo é ajudar projetos climáticos a atrair investimentos, entregar reduções de emissões mensuráveis e contribuir para o desenvolvimento econômico sustentável. Taha Meli Arvas comentou que mercados de carbono eficazes exigem mais do que plataformas de negociação, dependendo, em vez disso, de padrões confiáveis, processos transparentes e participantes com conhecimento e capacidade para atuar com segurança. Ele afirmou que a cooperação com o GCC visa explorar novas oportunidades de negociação de créditos de carbono, fortalecer a expertise técnica e apoiar o desenvolvimento do mercado em linha com as prioridades regulatórias da Turquia e as necessidades cambiantes do mercado. O acordo reflete um interesse comum em fortalecer o ecossistema de mercado de carbono da Turquia por meio de padrões reconhecidos internacionalmente, cooperação técnica e intercâmbio de expertise. Ao combinar a certificação de carbono com a operação de mercados organizados, o GCC e a EPIAS buscam apoiar mecanismos de mercado confiáveis e acessíveis capazes de traduzir compromissos climáticos em resultados mensuráveis.

artigo.texto: Samsung SDI – AI data center backup battery wins CES 2027 Innovation Award Samsung SDI’s space-saving UPS battery for AI data centers earned a 2027 CES Innovation Award for power, energy density and fire safety. Samsung SDI’s prismatic battery solution for uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems won the 2027 CES Innovation Award for the world’s largest electronics trade show set to take place in Las Vegas in January. The Korean battery maker said Tuesday its SDI U8A3-UPS, an uninterruptible power supply that provides emergency power to critical facilities like AI data centers during blackouts, won in the enterprise tech category. The system was recognized for its very high power output, high energy density and fire safety, Samsung SDI said. It uses prismatic cells made with lithium manganese oxide, which makes it 33 percent more space-efficient than conventional products, so fewer units are needed to deliver stable power. It can also supply backup power during sudden surges in demand from AI computing, which helps prevent server failures and data loss. artigo.texto: O leilão de reserva de capacidade marcado para 2 e 4 de dezembro coloca a sobra de eletricidade renovável no centro de uma disputa comercial entre Tesla, Petrobras e fabricantes chineses. Em 2025, o Brasil cortou ao menos 20% da geração eólica e solar, segundo a S&P Global, em um corte forçado conhecido como curtailment, provocado por falta de demanda ou de linhas para escoar a produção. O mundo instalou 108 GW em baterias em 2025, alta de 40% sobre o ano anterior, segundo a Agência Internacional de Energia (IEA). Esse avanço alimenta a corrida de grupos chineses contra Tesla e Petrobras num mercado estratégico para a transição elétrica da América do Sul. No Brasil, a matriz predominantemente hidráulica também conta com usinas reversíveis, que possuem dois reservatórios e cumprem papel semelhante ao de grandes baterias. O Ministério de Minas e Energia separou os certames: em 2 de dezembro, o leilão com exigência de conteúdo local; em 4 de dezembro, o aberto a todos os fornecedores. O relatório global do Schneider Electric Research Institute (SERI), “System Costs of Electricity: A new Baseline for the 21st Century Economy”, analisou 40.500 combinações de custos envolvendo geração solar, baterias e rede elétrica. A conclusão é que a integração entre painéis e armazenamento pode diminuir o gasto total do sistema em até 40% nos anos 2030, com os custos projetados, desde que a eletrificação da demanda avance junto, com data centers, veículos elétricos e bombas de calor. Quando a nova demanda ocupa a capacidade liberada pelas baterias, os custos fixos se dividem por um volume maior de energia vendida, derrubando o preço por megawatt-hora. Se oferta e consumo não crescerem em sintonia, os custos podem subir temporariamente antes de cair. O relatório ainda mostra que a duração dos equipamentos importa. Se os tempos de armazenamento empregados em diferentes ativos forem incompatíveis, o gasto total do sistema pode ficar até 35% acima do patamar atual. Tesla e BYD confirmaram interesse no leilão, que também terá Petrobras, Auren, Eneva e Weg, segundo o portal Zigg. Mais de 6 mil projetos foram cadastrados. No mercado brasileiro, a Voltxs aposta na locação de sistemas de armazenamento (BESS), em vez da venda, para reduzir o custo inicial das empresas. O modelo, segundo a empresa, permite adotar baterias sem grande desembolso inicial. Nos períodos de tarifa reduzida, o sistema guarda eletricidade e a entrega quando o preço aumenta, diminuindo a fatura de demanda contratada. Entre os clientes potenciais estão indústrias, data centers, shoppings, hospitais, aeroportos, agronegócio, mineração e centros logísticos. A disputa agendada para 2 e 4 de dezembro será o primeiro teste em escala nacional desse arranjo. O sucesso dependerá de alinhar oferta, consumo e financiamento, enquanto o setor acompanha se as baterias convertem o excedente em ativo econômico.

artigo.texto: Solar and battery storage can do a lot of the heavy lifting in a renewable electricity system. Add wind, and supplying reliable power gets nearly 20% cheaper, according to new analysis from energy think tank Ember. Wind fills gaps when solar output drops, so the system needs fewer batteries to keep electricity flowing. Ember’s analysis, produced with the Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC), found that adding wind to solar and battery storage cuts the median cost of meeting 90% of electricity demand from $105 to $86 per megawatt-hour. The median cost of solar and wind power covering all demand is $89/MWh, with batteries and a little backup. More wind means fewer batteries Solar and wind don’t follow the same schedule. Their output varies by time of day and across seasons, allowing one to offset the other’s shortfalls. That matters because storing enough electricity to get through a long stretch of weak solar output gets expensive. Wind reduces the amount of energy the batteries need to store in the first place. In the US, adding wind reduces the modeled battery requirement to meet 90% of demand from 20 hours of electricity use to 12 hours. Europe sees the same reduction, while China’s requirement falls from 18 hours to 12. The savings also put cheaper renewable power within reach of more regions. With wind included, regions that account for 75% of global electricity demand can meet 90% of their electricity demand at less than $100/MWh. With solar and batteries alone, that share is only 50%. “We already know that solar and wind are cheap,” said Daan Walter, principal at Ember. By combining solar, wind, and batteries, we can deliver reliable power at remarkably low costs almost everywhere in the world. That’s a pretty fundamental shift in the economics of energy. What happens when it’s cloudy and still? The researchers also looked at prolonged periods of low output. Globally, weighted by electricity demand, a week of low solar output occurs roughly four times a year. A week in which both solar and wind output are low occurs only about once every four years. That’s a global average, so individual locations will have different experiences. Ember defines a lull as seven consecutive days of output below half the source’s average. Combining wind and solar reduces the gaps in low output. New coal and gas doesn’t make financial sense The findings also raise questions for developers planning new fossil fuel plants. Ember identifies 845 GW of coal and gas capacity in planning worldwide. Adding wind raises the share located in regions where solar, wind, and battery storage can meet 90% of demand for under $100/MWh from 71% to 90%. In China alone, wind brings another 91 GW of planned coal and gas capacity into the range where renewables are cheaper. Include backup to cover all demand, and 706 GW of the planned fossil fuel capacity sits in regions where the renewable-based alternative costs less than $100/MWh. Without wind, that figure falls to 520 GW. For investors financing fossil fuel plants in the pipeline that are expected to run for decades, there is likely already a cheaper renewable alternative available to meet the same electricity demand, so it’s worth scrutinizing the project’s economics. artigo.texto: Botswana battery storage plan puts 100MWh beside the Mmadinare solar cluster Botswana Power Corporation has published plans for a 25MW battery with 100MWh of storage beside the Mmadinare solar cluster, with the World Bank funding its construction, as Botswana presents a climate plan at COP31 in Antalya that ranks energy generation as its largest opportunity for carbon market activity. Botswana Power Corporation has published a revised environmental and social management plan, dated 6 November, for a battery storage system of 25MW and 100MWh in 20 battery containers and five power conversion units, to be built on 2 hectares of a 40-hectare plot 8km south-east of Mmadinare in the Bobirwa District, beside the 100MW Mmadinare Solar PV Cluster. The plan, submitted to the Department of Environmental Protection in Selebi Phikwe, says the World Bank will fund the initial construction, pencilled in for 2027 over 9 to 12 months, and that the battery is designed to firm the output of the adjoining solar cluster and to provide peak-shaving and frequency services for the region. More than 243,288MWh had flowed into the grid from the solar cluster by its official launch on 31 August, with availability and reliability above 99% since operations began, according to BPC’s Chief Executive, David Kgoboko. Scatec, the Norwegian IPP that built and owns the plant, sells its power to BPC under a 25-year power purchase agreement. Solar plants at Bobonong, Phakalane, Shakawe and Mmadinare produced about 82,520MWh in the first quarter of 2026, or 9.1% of domestic generation against 3.2% a year earlier, by Statistics Botswana’s figures reported in Mmegi, while imports fell 29.8% on the previous quarter and the Morupule A and B coal plants supplied 90.8% of local generation. Under its revised Integrated Resource Plan the government wants renewables to supply 50% of the generation mix by 2030, up from about 8%, and in April President Duma Boko broke ground at Maun on a 500MW solar plant with a 500MWh battery, which BPC is executing with Okavango Solar under a government-to-government partnership with Oman and a 30-year power purchase agreement. The World Bank’s Renewable Energy Support and Access Accelerator project, approved in July 2024 with an $88 million loan and $34 million in Green Climate Fund finance, includes 50MW of utility-scale battery storage. Botswana’s third nationally determined contribution, which its delegation is presenting at COP31 in Antalya, rates energy generation as having the “largest” potential for carbon market activities and nature-based removals a “significant” one, with bushfire management and refrigerant transitions at “moderate” and a “lower volume” expected from energy efficiency, according to Argus. Its draft carbon market framework, which Carbon Pulse reported the plan targets for the first quarter of 2027, would keep the cheaper mitigation for Botswana’s own target and offer the higher-cost activities abroad as internationally transferred mitigation outcomes under Article 6, and it names both Article 6.2 and the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism as suitable routes for energy generation. Mitigation under the unconditional target will need $224 million between 2026 and 2035, the NDC says, and the conditional mitigation need for the same period is $1.5 billion. The second NDC, submitted in December 2024, had put the conditional need to 2030 at $2.7 billion, of which about $50 million has been secured, Argus reported. On removals, the NDC cautions against overselling the low-cost mitigation Botswana needs for its own unconditional target, and the government will seek $4.32 billion in climate finance at COP31, the state news agency BOPA reported. Before commissioning, the battery will need grid-connection and regulatory approvals from the Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority, the ESMP says, and amendments to BERA’s own Act that would recognise independent transmission providers and introduce electricity trading are due in Parliament’s November sitting, according to Mmegi’s report of remarks by BERA’s Chief Executive, Never Tshabang, at the National Business Conference in Francistown in October. Fieldwork for the ESMP found no one living on the 40-hectare plot that the Ngwato Land Board allocated to BPC, so no resettlement plan is needed, and the battery compound will fence about 2 hectares, leaving the other 38 open for the livestock of neighbouring farmers and for the communities who collect non-timber forest products there.

artigo.texto: Moratorium? Tax break? Colorado cities face data center policy choices As data centers continue to pop up across Colorado, municipalities are facing a difficult choice: weighing the economic benefits against growing concerns from the communities they serve. While some municipalities are passing moratoriums on data centers, Douglas County leaders recently granted a $19 million tax break in business personal property taxes to a new Flexential data center that's under construction in Parker. That data center is set to open next year. Across Colorado, community members have been saying no to data centers. "A lot of people feel very blindsided about the data centers popping up, and so they don't feel heard, which I understand, and I understand their disappointment," one Douglas County resident said in a recent meeting. "We needed this moratorium, and you all failed us, and you failed yourselves," an Aurora resident said in another meeting. Residents have shared worries about water, electricity, noise and pollution. "I'm scared for the water, scared for the pollution, scared for my air, my quality of life. The noise that this data center might create- that's why I'm so disappointed in this," one Colorado resident recently said. But one CEO in the rapidly growing industry says data centers are a necessity in modern life. Flexential's CEO and a public policy expert weighed in on the heated debate surrounding them. "Your connected life can't happen without a data center," said Ryan Mallory, CEO of Flexential. "All of the social media apps that you're using run through our sites, as well as a lot of the streaming services that everybody's using at home." Headquartered in Denver, Flexential has data centers across the country. Its fifth Colorado center is in development in Parker. "This is an industrial shell that has power and cooling that customers can then put their own IT infrastructure into," Mallory said. While Mallory says AI-focused customers only make up 11% of Flexential's centers, he says AI data centers are fueling the U.S.'s economic growth right now. "The GDP in the United States is growing about 3%, 3.5%. That's fueled primarily by AI infrastructure data centers," Mallory said. But with communities mobilizing against them, how should local leaders respond? "It's a lot of hard and fast feelings," said Billy Wynn, the lead author of a recent report on data centers, prepared by the Romer Institute of Evidence-Based Policy for the city of Colorado Springs. "It's a very nascent and kind of burgeoning issue," Wynne said. The report recommends municipalities handle data center applications with transparency, invite the public to participate and develop standard rules and processes. "Do it in a transparent way, develop policies that are broadly applicable, not case by case, ad hoc negotiations. Give the public a bona fide opportunity to express their interests, concerns, questions," Wynne said. "[We] really want to be treating different facilities as similarly as much as possible." It also recommends clarifying evidence-based standards around water and energy use. Mallory says Flexential uses an efficient closed-loop system rather than evaporative cooling. "Our site in Parker will use the same amount of water as about six homes," Mallory said. He says data centers bring tax revenue that can be beneficial for communities. Wynne says there are a lot of unknowns in the rapidly changing space, and evidence should guide communities weighing data centers. "Let's do our best to look at the facts, and then have a more informed debate about it," Wynne said. Flexential's CEO also spoke on the impact of the recent election on data center buildout after the stock market plummeted following the midterms. While Mallory attributes that to standard volatility, he does think that Democratic lawmakers could slow data center permitting and buildout. "At the end of the day, the people that lose out isn't going to be Flexential. It's going to be the communities that we serve," Mallory said.

artigo.texto: Bangladesh, Singapore sign MoU on carbon market cooperation Speaking at the signing ceremony, Faridul Islam said Bangladesh warmly welcomes the partnership with Singapore under the Paris Agreement. Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance cooperation in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, opening up new opportunities for climate financing and joint initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The MoU was signed this morning (14 November) at the Singapore Pavilion on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, said to a press release. State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam signed the agreement on behalf of Bangladesh, while Secretary of Singapore's Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment Melvin Ong signed for his country. The agreement is expected to facilitate Bangladesh's participation in international carbon markets, expand access to carbon financing and environmentally sustainable investments, and support the implementation of the country's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0). Speaking at the signing ceremony, Faridul Islam said Bangladesh warmly welcomes the partnership with Singapore under the Paris Agreement. He said the cooperation would help unlock new opportunities for carbon finance, develop high-quality and transparent carbon markets, and advance the implementation of Bangladesh's NDC 3.0. Bangladesh is committed to working closely with Singapore to promote sustainable development, achieve ambitious climate goals and strengthen effective global climate action, he added. Under the MoU, the two countries will exchange information, knowledge and experience on carbon credits and explore further cooperation in greenhouse gas emission reduction projects based on mutual interests and benefits. The partnership is expected to accelerate climate change mitigation efforts by utilising the opportunities for international cooperation provided under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. It is also expected to support the development of internationally recognised carbon markets in Bangladesh, facilitate the transfer of climate-friendly technologies, attract greater private sector investment and create new avenues for international climate finance. The initiative will further contribute to Bangladesh's transition towards sustainable and low-carbon development and help achieve its national climate targets.

artigo.texto: Our Next Energy Inc. (ONE), a Novi-based U.S. energy storage technology company and battery manufacturer, has signed an agreement with New York’s Wen Acquisition Corp. to take ONE public and trade on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol ONEE. “Over the last five years, LFP (lithium iron phosphate) has grown from roughly 20 percent to 60 percent of the global battery market, yet China produces approximately 99 percent of the world’s LFP cells,” says Mujeeb Ijaz, founder and CEO of ONE. “We built ONE to close that gap with a secure American and allied supply chain. “We believe our combination with Wen will give us a public platform to scale ONE into this $40 billion addressable market with access to growth capital as we scale our operations to meet rising demand.” Most LFP cells made in America today come from foreign-owned factories or rely on licensed Chinese technology. ONE uses its own domestic technology, from electrode active materials through fully integrated energy storage systems. Two recent federal actions make that distinction matter, according to ONE. The FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) extends battery restrictions to cells and components produced by a foreign entity of concern (FEOC) or under FEOC technology licenses. Executive Order 14421, signed in August 2026, restricts battery energy storage systems and other grid equipment tied to covered foreign entities from the U.S. bulk-power system. ONE says it’s well positioned to meet this moment. It makes its cells in Van Buren Township and integrates them in Novi with its own battery management systems (BMS) into packs and containerized energy storage systems for defense, rail, and grid customers that require safety, durability, and a secure domestic supply chain. “ONE has done the hard part of building an American LFP cell and pack business, with factories operating and customers in markets that increasingly require domestic supply,” says Julian Sevillano, CEO of Wen. “With two operating factories, binding customer contracts, and federal policy appearing to move its way, ONE is positioned to lead the reshoring of critical battery manufacturing in the United States.” The boards of directors of both Wen and ONE have approved the proposed transaction, which is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to approval by Wen’s shareholders and ONE’s stockholders and the satisfaction of other customary closing conditions, including Wen’s registration statement on Form S-4 being declared effective by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (HSR Act) and the satisfaction or waiver of a minimum cash condition. Additional information about the proposed transaction, including a copy of the business combination agreement, will be provided in a Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed by Wen with the SEC and available at sec.gov. For more information about ONE, visit one.ai.

artigo.texto: O Brasil pode perder para o exterior a próxima onda de investimentos em data centers. A conclusão saiu de um painel em Lisboa que juntou a ANP, a agência que regula petróleo, gás natural e biocombustíveis, e a Eneva, do mercado de gás e energia, em torno das regras tributárias e energéticas do setor. O calendário aperta. Interlocutores ouvidos pela Agência iNFRA relatam que as tratativas dentro do Executivo avançaram e que o decreto do Redata, o Regime Especial de Tributação voltado aos Serviços de Data Center, deve sair ainda em novembro. Falta pacificar, porém, o ponto mais espinhoso do setor elétrico. Uma das hipóteses na mesa obriga os empreendimentos a contratar energia nova para se abastecer, exigência batizada de adicionalidade energética. Quem deu o tom do alerta foi Pietro Mendes, diretor da ANP, na Conferência Ibero-Brasileira de Energia (Coniben) 2026, em Lisboa, segundo apuração do site especializado Megawhat. Ele cobrou do governo federal celeridade para fechar as regras definitivas do programa. Na avaliação dele, o país já parte em desvantagem na disputa global por novos hubs de processamento de dados. Segundo ele, o país vai perdendo oportunidades e investimentos, e o capital acaba indo para outro lugar. O gás natural já consta da legislação do programa. Mendes, porém, criticou duas ideias em circulação, a de condicionar a participação das térmicas à captura e ao armazenamento de carbono e a de priorizar o biometano no abastecimento. A captura de carbono serve para mitigar os impactos da queima de combustíveis fósseis, mas vira barreira se transformada em obrigação, avaliou o diretor. Sobre o biometano, ele reconheceu papel relevante na transição energética e lembrou o limite atual, uma produção sem escala para usinas de grande porte. Critérios rígidos demais, na mesma leitura, castigariam o gás num país cuja matriz elétrica já tem peso enorme de fontes renováveis. Diretrizes engessadas, completou, espantam investidores internacionais de grande porte. O contraponto veio de Christiano Vieira, diretor de Regulação da Eneva. Para ele, a regulamentação precisa ir além da origem limpa da eletricidade contratada e contabilizar o custo de manter o abastecimento garantido. Data centers exigem eletricidade sem pausa, enquanto sol e vento variam ao longo do dia. Para Vieira, não faz sentido montar um modelo energético só com renováveis e deixar a conta da segurança do abastecimento para todos os usuários do sistema. O executivo defendeu preservar as metas de descarbonização e abrir caminho para que os empreendedores ofereçam potência e confiabilidade a preços competitivos, de térmicas a gás a sistemas de armazenamento. Citou empreendimentos que demandam entre 300 MW e 500 MW, escala que exige reforço no fornecimento. Baterias ajudam a dar qualidade à energia usada em aplicações de inteligência artificial. Não bastam, ponderou Vieira, para sustentar o funcionamento ininterrupto que os empreendimentos exigem. O decreto esperado para ainda este mês vai arbitrar o equilíbrio entre descarbonização, segurança de suprimento e custo. Errar a mão, na avaliação do diretor da ANP, empurra o capital para a concorrência internacional.

artigo.texto: - Owner’s-side partner will manage both ERCOT projects through commissioning to commercial operation date (COD), slated for 2027, strengthening grid resilience and helping lower power prices for Texas consumers. - Project wins build on boutique energy services firm’s expanding BESS portfolio in the Southwestern U.S. AUSTIN, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Charge Power Inc.—the hands-on, owner’s-side energy storage partner—today announced it was awarded two battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Texas to manage through commissioning: a 150-megawatt (MW) / 300-megawatt-hour (MWh) project and a 140 MW / 280 MWh project. Together, the projects will add 290 MW / 580 MWh of storage capacity to the ERCOT grid as Charge Power continues to build out its footprint in the rapidly expanding Southwestern U.S. energy storage market. On both projects, expected to reach commercial operation in 2027, Charge Power will integrate EPC contractors, project engineers, suppliers, documentation, and the ERCOT interconnection checklist—among other parties and processes—on the owner’s behalf. Its role is to close gaps in project delivery so that projects energize on time and earn from day one. During Charge Power’s involvement, both projects are also onboarding the WARAM platform for project governance, due diligence, and compliance. WARAM connects physical energy-asset requirements to the evidence that proves them, keeping that record current through ownership, certification, and transfer. “Texas is one of the most demanding storage markets in the country, and the stretch between construction and commercial operation is where a project either protects its returns or loses them,” said Ravi Pinnelli, founder and president of Charge Power. “We approach every project with an owner-operator mindset, so on these projects our decisions prioritize schedule, revenue, and long-term performance the way the owner would. Through shifting markets and an evolving energy landscape, our goal is to deliver execution certainty from day one to COD and beyond.” The wins extend Charge Power’s track record of protecting project outcomes for BESS owners. Since its founding in 2022, the company has commissioned 3 gigawatts (GW) / 7 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage, and its hands-on approach has saved owners more than $10 million in estimated avoided liquidated damages. Charge Power’s recent project awards come as energy storage demand in Texas continues to surge. Battery capacity on the ERCOT grid roughly doubled each year from 2020 through 2024 and grew another 76% in 2025, reaching 16.5 GW / 28.8 GWh by the end of June 2026, according to Modo Energy. Utility-scale storage captures lower-cost power when it is plentiful on the grid and delivers it when demand peaks, reducing the cost of power for consumers, cutting reliance on carbon-heavy peaker plants, and strengthening grid reliability. Batteries also respond in milliseconds to stabilize the grid and help it ride through extreme weather and sudden plant outages. According to an American Clean Power Association analysis, in Texas alone, storage deployed since 2023 has saved consumers over $750 million in electricity costs. About Charge Power Charge Power is the independent, hands-on, owner’s-side partner for energy storage. A boutique energy services firm with offices in Austin, Texas and Toronto, the company approaches every project with an owner-operator mindset from design through commissioning and beyond. It closes the gaps between contractors during project delivery, keeping everything aligned on the owner’s behalf, so projects energize on time and earn from day one. As a battery energy storage system (BESS) specialist with deep grid and market expertise, Charge Power optimizes long-term performance and fixes small problems before they become expensive ones, preserving revenue and uptime—and protecting project outcomes. The result: execution certainty in an evolving energy landscape. Founded in 2022 by BESS industry veterans, Charge Power has commissioned 3 GW / 7 GWh of energy storage across U.S. energy markets — including CAISO, ERCOT, MISO and PJM — as well as Canada, India, Japan and the U.K. Learn more at www.chargepowerinc.com. A photo accompanying this announcement is available at https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/bfcf648e-9e62-4fc7-b864-ad0ce895e8dc Media contact Chris Larson Media Communications chris.larson@chargepowerinc.com Media gallery

artigo.texto: O Brasil está abraçando uma oportunidade que ninguém quer deixar escapar. Com investimentos bilionários anunciados, a expansão acelerada da inteligência artificial e a crescente importância da capacidade computacional, atrair grandes data centers virou uma aposta de desenvolvimento econômico e tecnológico. Mas a pressa para entrar nessa corrida pode estar passando por cima de uma avaliação criteriosa sobre os ganhos e principalmente sobre as perdas para o país. Essa conta começa pelo que o conceito de "nuvem" esconde. O uso da IA mobiliza servidores que demandam muitíssima energia e refrigeração, apoiados em instalações que ocupam território e dependem de redes elétricas e de fontes de água. Por isso, a conveniência digital tem uma contrapartida material e ambiental. Esse tema ganhou outra dimensão durante o 2º Seminário de Inteligência Artificial, Meio Ambiente e Justiça Socioambiental, organizado pelo Lapin (Laboratório de Políticas Públicas e Internet) em Fortaleza, entre os dias 8 e 10. A programação incluiu uma visita ao território Anacé, nas proximidades do Complexo Industrial e Portuário do Pecém, onde está sendo construído um grande data center para o TikTok. Assim, a discussão deixou de ser apenas sobre tecnologia e ganhou endereço e rostos. Essa promessa foi encampada pelas propostas dos principais candidatos à presidência da República, incluindo as de Lula. Ampliar a capacidade computacional, desenvolver serviços de IA, estimular pesquisa e gerar empregos qualificados são objetivos legítimos. Mas investimentos bilionários não garantem, por si só, benefícios distribuídos nem ganhos tecnológicos proporcionais aos recursos que o Brasil oferece. Nos Estados Unidos, governos locais já impõem restrições aos data centers. Se quem recebe esses empreendimentos há mais tempo começa a impor limites, o Brasil precisa entender que questionamentos não representam necessariamente oportunidades perdidas, fazendo parte de uma busca pelo equilíbrio necessário. Veja esse artigo em vídeo: Esse equilíbrio exige questionar a ideia de que temos energia limpa sobrando. Nossa matriz elétrica é predominantemente renovável, mas há cortes por limitações da rede, segurança operacional e falta de demanda em certos horários. De janeiro a abril de 2026, eles atingiram 2.843 MW médios de geração eólica e solar, sendo 2.233 MW no Nordeste. Essa energia desperdiçada não pode ser automaticamente direcionada aos data centers, pois isso depende da localização, da capacidade da rede e de novos investimentos em transmissão e conexão. Além disso, data centers precisam dissipar o calor dos equipamentos e algumas tecnologias de refrigeração consomem volumes expressivos de água. Mesmo nos mais modernos, não basta medir a eficiência hídrica, pois uma instalação grande pode ter baixo consumo relativo e ainda retirar muita água do local. No Pecém, além da captação subterrânea, o projeto prevê 120 geradores de emergência a diesel, entre outros impactos sobre o território. - Assine gratuitamente minha newsletter sobre IA, experiência do cliente, mídia e transformação digital - Inscreva-se no meu podcast (escolha a plataforma): Spotify, Deezer, Apple Podcasts ou Soundcloud No dia 15 de setembro, o Brasil instituiu o Redata, regime que reduz tributos sobre equipamentos em troca de pesquisa no país, atendimento ao mercado interno, uso de energia renovável ou de baixa emissão e eficiência hídrica. Mas parte dos critérios depende de regulamentação, e é preciso demonstrar que o retorno público justifica a enorme vantagem privada. "Quando o governo fala de soberania digital e acha que trazer data centers para o território é garantia de soberania, ele está errado", afirma Cynthia Picolo, diretora-executiva do Lapin. Ela distingue as meras presenças físicas do controle sobre suas finalidades, a gestão dos recursos naturais e a governança. "Ter a infraestrutura no território não é o mesmo que controlá-la." Soberania também exige respeitar quem vive no território. Os Anacé afirmam que seu protocolo de consulta não foi respeitado, enquanto o Ministério Público Federal e a Defensoria Pública da União questionam a suficiência do licenciamento daquele data center. Ao defender a repartição justa de benefícios, a defensora pública Thalita Verônica ressaltou durante o evento que "isso não se confunde com escola, estrada, água potável, que já são uma obrigação do Estado". Fazendo do jeito certo Não se trata, portanto, de rejeitar a tecnologia ou de impedir investimentos, mas de estabelecer as condições para que eles beneficiem o país respeitando os direitos da população. "Para mim, é possível atrair data centers de uma forma sustentável, ética e segura", explica Edson Prestes, professor da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul. "Mas, para isso, a gente não pode 'colocar a carroça na frente dos bois'." Isso começa antes da aprovação e dos incentivos, avaliando a disponibilidade de água, a capacidade elétrica, a vegetação, as áreas protegidas e os direitos das comunidades tradicionais. Não basta examinar o terreno do data center, sendo necessário avaliar toda a infraestrutura que o sustenta e os impactos somados aos de outros empreendimentos. O licenciamento deve exigir estudos proporcionais ao porte e ao potencial de impacto, com participação pública. E a fiscalização não pode terminar na licença. As empresas envolvidas devem divulgar dados verificáveis sobre consumo e eficiência no uso de água e de energia, emissões e resíduos. Picolo defende o acompanhamento dos efeitos da disputa por recursos sobre as comunidades e outras atividades locais. Cabe ao poder público fiscalizar impactos e contrapartidas durante toda a operação, com verificação independente dos dados apresentados. Além disso, o investimento só se transforma em desenvolvimento quando deixa conhecimento e capacidade no país. artigo.texto: Stem and Copec Expand Partnership to Advance Energy Storage and Intelligent Energy Management Across Latin America Building on the Granja Solar project in Chile, the companies will jointly serve utility-scale and commercial and industrial customers across key regional markets HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 2026-- Stem, Inc. (NYSE: STEM), a global leader in AI-enabled clean energy software and services, today announced a partnership agreement with Copec Flux, the renewable energy subsidiary of Copec S.A., to jointly deliver energy storage and energy management solutions, initially focusing on Chile, with plans to explore opportunities in Colombia and other Latin American markets. The agreement expands an existing relationship established through the Granja Solar project in Chile, where Copec Flux is deploying Stem's PowerTrack™ Energy Management System (EMS) as the master control system for a 135 MW solar facility being retrofitted with a 420 MWh battery energy storage system. Announced in May 2026, the project provides a foundation for extending the companies' collaboration to additional customers and markets. “Our partnership with Copec Flux is about making advanced energy technology more accessible to customers while simplifying how projects are deployed and operated,” said Arun Narayanan, Chief Executive Officer of Stem. “By combining our technology with Copec Flux's local capabilities, we can help customers bring projects online faster, improve operational performance, and maximize the long-term value of their energy investments.” Under the partnership, Stem will provide its PowerTrack software and controls technology, including EMS, power plant controls (PPC), and cloud-based monitoring and analytics, while Copec Flux will lead local engineering, project delivery, and operational services. The joint offering will serve utility-scale developers and asset owners as well as commercial and industrial (C&I) customers, providing a coordinated approach to deploying, monitoring, and managing solar, storage, and hybrid energy assets. “Energy storage is becoming critical for reliability across regional grids,” said Juan Cristóbal González, CEO of Copec Flux. “Collaborating with specialized technology providers like Stem allows us to test software capabilities at Granja Solar and identify the most efficient ways to support our clients' energy needs.” The expanded relationship reflects Stem's broader strategy to grow its international footprint through partnerships that combine its software and controls capabilities with established regional providers. As demand for flexible, intelligent energy infrastructure continues to grow, the companies see opportunities to extend the delivery model established at Granja Solar to additional projects and customers throughout Latin America. For more information on Stem and the PowerTrack, visit stem.com. About Stem Stem is a global leader in energy intelligence and the operating system for clean energy: where assets connect, sites are optimized, and value is captured. Powered by decades of operational experience and purpose-built AI, our PowerTrack™ platform is the layer that sits between raw data and confident action, making every decision-maker smarter, every asset more productive, and every transition more certain. From asset monitoring to portfolio optimization and control, PowerTrack delivers everything energy professionals need in one place. With projects managed across 55 countries, we have spent nearly 20 years empowering asset owners, operators, and developers to take command of what comes next, with the certainty to act, the trust to commit, and the intelligence to lead. Learn more at stem.com. About Copec and Copec Flux Copec is one of Chile's leading energy companies, with nearly 90 years of experience serving individuals, businesses, and industries across the country. Historically recognized for its leadership in fuel distribution and convenience services, the company is evolving into a broader energy and mobility platform, with growing investments in renewable energy, electromobility, and energy storage. As part of this strategy, its subsidiary Copec Flux develops, builds, and operates solar and energy storage projects across Chile, delivering integrated clean energy solutions for utility-scale, commercial, and industrial customers. Through its nationwide footprint, operational capabilities, and long-term commitment to innovation and sustainability, Copec seeks to play a key role in accelerating Chile’s energy transition and development.
